# Chapter 14: Spacewalk Under Fire

Commander Leo Mercer gripped the padded edges of the extravehicular lock hatch with trembling fingers, trying not to look at the looming singularity devouring billions of kilometers of star-strewn wilderness outside the viewing portals. The white noise static of the life support systems masked most other sounds, but beneath that eerie blankness he heard—faintly—the highpitched whine of pumps charging his EVA suit to nominal operating pressure. It was an indistinguishable hum among the cacophony of life signs beeping and flashing indicator lights, a constant reminder that only a thin layer of superstrength polymer and pressurized air separated him from venturing out into suffocating darkness with no return.

"You sure about this, Astrid?"

The skipper flashed him a smirk from where she stood rigidly opposite, mirrored visor reflecting the frantic activity within his helmet like the polished convex surface of sunglasses. "Not just sure – excited. Who gets to play space chicken with the mother of all black holes everyday? Hell, I might even get my first close-up glimpse of those spooky accretion disk winds. What do you say, Leo - ready to dip our toes in eternity?"

Leo barely managed a snort through thinned lips. Ready as he'd ever be to stare Armageddon in the face... He slid the outer seal closed with a reassuring thunk, feeling the chill vacuum seep through the sealant as the interior atmosphere equalized at a mere few percent oxygen partial pressure.

"Don't let me forget to send some prayers to whichever deity you worship," he muttered wryly.

"Sarcasm noted," Astrid replied dryly, tapping her temple – supposedly a neural link to something resembling a deity according to Corsair lore. Whether genuine faith or cleverly crafted bluff remained anyone's guess. All that mattered was whether whatever force granted her crew such audacious luck held sway for them once more. If so...

"We've got fifteen minutes to defuse this fire," Astrid said, cutting the tension and gesture at the critical status display flashing red amidst a sea of amber warnings illuminating the cockpit control panels.

As if on cue, the bridge erupted in a symphony of klaxons and flashing lights - the ship itself shrieking its distress amid mounting heat and approaching critical failure. With only seconds left on the countdown timer, Astrid slammed open the inner hatch, pulling both of them out onto the exposed walkways surrounding the central command axis. She reached down, seized a cylindrical maintenance pod with one gloved hand, and hurled it at an angle across the bridge, watching with hawk-like focus as it tumbled forward in zero gravity before striking hard against the edge of an emergency shuttle bay door.

Leo watched in rapt attention as Astrid grabbed another pod from storage, spinning effortlessly on one toe as she prepared for launch herself. In this environment, without the artificial gravity fields that sustained human physiology on board ships, every movement required meticulous calculation and precision—lest one become the ship's worst enemy.

"Time's running out," she growled over the comms system, voice muffled slightly by the snug fit of her helmet and the background din of hissing valves and warbling alarm sirens. "Need you to cover my back on this one, commander. We're headed into the reactor compartment."

Mercer nodded curtly within the confines of his own helmet, hands working swiftly along the arm of his suit to unfold the grappling tether coiled there. Its thin yet nearly indestructible carbon fiber strands could withstand tens of thousands of gees' acceleration stress without failure—and likely far more under vacuum conditions if needed.

✦ ✦ ✦

Scene 2: Spacewalk Under Fire

The bridge erupted in chaos around them, strobing blue light casting eerie shadows as laser blasts sizzled through the thin hull plating. Astrid sprinted toward the gaping hole torn by Leo's earlier explosive decompression, propulsive muscles straining beneath her skintight spacesuit as she battled planetfall gravity while hauling twice her body weight in a portable air cylinder slung from her belt.

Leo scrambled after her, boots clomping heavily against the grated catwalks despite the best effort of his microgravity dampeners to approximate Earthlike traction. Ropes snagged behind him, trailing like a macramé snake, as he released his grip on the exposed structural members and lunged into the void beside Astrid. A gout of escaping gas belched past their heads, stinging eyes shut. They fell together, arms instinctively wrapping in a tight embrace as they drifted toward the damaged bulkhead.

Astrid shoved off a nearby surface just in time, her booted foot knocking the breath from Leo as she angled herself away from the jagged hole now yawning wide mere meters behind. Alarms wailed on and on—structural warnings, depressurization alerts, damage reports tumbling in from throughout the crippled hulk of the starship.

"What the fuck were you thinking, pilot boy?" Astrid snarled, her words distorted by crackling static in the suit comms. "You couldn't have waited five damn minutes?"

The anger in her tone jarred, a rare frison amidst the numbing terror and adrenaline pumping through Leo's veins. He glanced sidelong at Vex, noting the feral intensity burning in those icy blue eyes beneath a mask of carbon fiber faceplate—a look reserved only for battle situations where survival truly hung in the balance.

"Suffocated civilians wasn't enough?"
he retorted hotly.

A blast of searing wind buffeted them hard from above, almost ripping the safety line tethers still clinging desperately to their wrists. Together they pirouetted, limbs flailing wildly as they struggled to regain control in near-weightlessness.

Once stabilized again, Leo shot an accusing glare her way, hand gripping the rope like a taloned fist. "Your call, captain. You want to play hero and risk us both to secure that reactor core access? Fine. I'll cover your back, but don't expect me to follow orders blindly ever again under fire, understand? Not even yours."

Astrid paused, the faint red glow of reentry heat suffusing her suit as the ship grew hotter and hotter. After a moment's consideration, her features softened into a grim yet respectful expression—the kind reserved for an adversary acknowledged worthy, even in extremis.

"You did what you had to do back there," she allowed grudgingly beneath the helmet's metallic reverberations. "I wouldn't have hesitated either. Doesn't change the facts though, commander... we're not exactly on the same page when planetary politics collide with personal morals. It's gonna be real fucking interesting trying to navigate the moral implications of that explosive situation once we get to the bottom of who hired these bastards."

Leo bit back a savage retort threatening to tear loose in response, realizing with a jolt of trepidation that not only was this a struggle to align tactical goals, but also a battle being waged within Astrid herself—and potentially within himself, as well, given their vastly different backgrounds and ethics.

With new resolve, he faced forward again, squinting against the glare of distant starfires bleeding over the curvature of Kaida Prime below as the atmospheric shell thinned to a blue haze.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo Mercer's heart thundered as the tether rattled ominously, jerking him heedlessly closer to the Marauder's spinning hull. Sweat trickled beneath his goggles, stinging eyes already constricted by the solar radiance blazing mercilessly at near-orbital velocities. Just behind them, the disintegrating junk freighter flared into a brief, incandescent cinder before collapsing into streaks of ionized plasma.

Astrid Vex's voice cut through the screeching static as she struggled valiantly to restrain their wayward lifeline amidst the tempest raged by the rapidly thinning upper atmosphere:

"Damn it, damn it, hang on, I almost—got it! Fuck, that was too close!"

The momentum still sent both spacecraft spiraling uncontrollably as Astrid hastily locked off their tether reel, forcing Leo to anchor with hand-over-hand tugs down the haphazard rope whipping erratically around the asteroid field. His gloved fingers ached with each brutal grab amid the lacerating grit and razor splinters scoured raw from their impact crater.

"You good out there?" Astrid asked tightly while wrestling with the ship at his end, her words clipped from sheer effort over comms lost in the howling maelstrom between them.

Leo risked a glance toward the tumbling freighter's skeletal remains and turned away from the searing light of Kaidaprine's ascending sun blazing like a miniature supernova. The planet's cobalt seas and emerald forests shimmered tantalizingly visible beyond the translucent veil of atmosphere already consumed by superheated gas and molten rock.

"Not great," Leo replied hoarsely, grunting as another particularly vicious jolt tore his grip nearly loose before locking down again on the frayed line above him. "But I'm here. What about the ship? Still on course?"

"Yeah, barely. Thrusters are shot, navigation's wonky, and I've got structural stress mounts climbing through the red zones," Astrid ground out. "But at least we managed to stay clear of whatever nukes they were planning to drop after us. Once we stabilize and reboot the AI, I'll start scouting repairs...if we don't get ourselves snared in this damned debris first."

She paused, exhaling a deep breath that puffed out mistily in the vacuum before continuing:

"If not for that lucky spin from your emergency jettison—sorry, couldn't resist—damn straight I owe you one now too. Maybe we should work on our team coordination sometime, huh?"

Leo resisted a chuckle despite the terror still gripping his guts. This woman really knew how to make an old flyboy's heart skip a beat during the most improbable flight of his life. When they finally managed to wrest free of the chaotic asteroids, limp exhausted against the airlock's magnetic catch after another nerve-wracking hour, he realized just how intimately entangled they'd become in more than just metal lines—and how much it pained him to realize their roles would be worlds apart someday soon...

Because regardless of their budding trust, or whatever other secrets they might cautiously reveal, one thing remained as certain as the unforgiving laws of gravity themselves—Ideals like theirs could never reconcile upon the kill-or-be-killed playing fields of the Rim's illicit fringes.

✦ ✦ ✦

The airlock released its magnetic hold as Leo drifted back into the Starlight Marauder under his own dwindling momentum. As he tumbled slowly toward the main compartment, lights reactivated across the ship's battered hull, casting strobing shadows across asteroid-scorched plates.

"Astrid? You okay?" Leo called over the intercom as he pressed himself against the outer hull, arms spread, and let his centrifugal motion wind down.

"We're...still coherent," Vex replied, her voice laced with exhaustion's brittle edge, echoing from the helm. A moment later, the hatch sealed shut behind him, its inner door sliding open with a pneumatic hiss.

Leo pushed off the cold surface, catching himself before colliding with his fellow survivor amidst the cramped airlock chamber. They locked eyes, gazes lingering briefly in a silent acknowledgment beyond spoken words - a shared understanding of the perils they'd faced and escaped, bound by threads thicker than any mere human connection ought to sustain.

Yet even then, beyond the confines of their beleaguered vessel, amidst the wreckage of what had once been stable orbits and star-spanning ambitions, Leo sensed the vast expanse stretching around them like an inscrutable titan awakening...

He glanced past Vex at the forward main viewer and gasped. Through the scratched acrylic, the distant spiral arms of the Whirlpool Galaxy pierced the blackness, galaxies, stars, and glowing nebulas sweeping across their viewport like spectral brushstrokes. Jupiter-sized crimson pulsars flanked the massive galaxy's core, beaming eerie cosmic rays and magnetically anchored radiation storms.

"Holy shit..." Leo breathed, his hands drifting involuntarily upward towards the unseen reaches of the universe without truly connecting. The breathtaking vista dwarfed every memory, accomplishment, or dream he'd ever had. Before this instant, his grasp of infinite scales was limited to theoretical equations and abstract simulations. Now, the very fabric of creation unspooled before his awestruck gaze.

"Try the sensors after we get the shields up," he suggested, reluctantly tearing his attention away to face reality, to salvage what bits they could manage here, there. There'll be no triumphant victory parades awaiting them back home...if they made it back at all. Only cold data to analyze, damaged pride to heal, and haunting thoughts of what might've been if fate hadn't cruelly jerked them both across lightyears to this unforgiving rim of civilization.

As the klaxons subsided from the last stages of post-impact diagnostics, quiet fell across the bridge. Astrid broke the oppressive silence:

"Looks like our long-range transponder took a direct hit. Anything we beam back will be pinging for days until someone finds the distress frequency buried amongst the noise..."

Leo nodded grimly, knowing full well what those long, agonizing days would mean if rescued. Even with all the medical marvels back Earthside, the toll of prolonged hibernation and the mysteries they ported in from the future - whether cursed alien nanotech or temporal anomalies that ate entire fleets, leaving only whisper-thin ripples of quantum decay - they likely would never step foot again on the soil of Sol-Three. Any hope of rekindling lives already lived on Terra, of reconnecting bonds with families who must have mourned their loss eons ago, slipped further away with each passing orbit of the dead world below.

Their journey would forge them anew, perhaps into legends whispered in hushed bars on forgotten colony worlds, but at the cost of forever being cut off not only from loved ones but from everything humanity held dear about itself - history woven from myth and reality, laughter in sun-d.

# Chapter 15: The Magnetar Flare

Captain Astrid Vex Ross's eyes flashed open, unclouded even by the afterimages of the proximity alarm strobes that had stabbed through her pupils half a breath prior. Reflexively, she snapped her gaze to the viewports spanning the curved forward bulkhead, instantly seeking confirmation or disavowal of the danger that had spurred her to react with such swift, instinctive violence. Her mind and body, honed over centuries by countless battles fought under a dozen solar systems, performed the rapid threat assessment as smoothly and reflexively as the hum of her cybernetic limbs.

At first glance, nothing seemed amiss. No missiles flared on infrared scanning grids or streaked trails marred the abyssal blackness outside. But then Astrid's trained awareness picked up the cues — the sudden absence of warmth radiation emanating from the crippled destroyer hovering in the distance, its shattered hull glistening like a vast shard of splintered jade against the stars; the eerie stillness that settled over the battlefield when all sound waves were leeched by the void; and, worst of all, the flatline silence of her starboard radar display, once a dancing tapestry of friendlies, foes, and neutrals, now merely a cold, inert slate devoid of any echoes, pulsing signals, or warning markers.

Astrid's hand shot out, clamping onto the wrist of her tactical officer, Lieutenant Zara Krieghof. The young woman, despite sharing her commanding officer's shock at this sudden information blackout, maintained professional composure and met Astrid's gaze straight on. "Radar's gone dark, ma'am. So has long-range scanner and the sensor lattice. Looks like the magnetic field of that nearby blue giant surged big-time."

"We're blind, then," Astrid grated through clenched teeth. She watched as Zara frantically worked her console, firing frantic pulses towards their closest allies on the far horizon, silently praying that some of the signals would pierce whatever electromagnetic tempest now besieged their instruments. Astrid could feel the crew's tension mounting, a palpable presence heavy enough to settle in her lungs, but she suppressed any flicker of panic. Experience had taught her that in situations like these, calm decisive action was required, not a commander's screams and threats. 

Her attention was then drawn to the main viewscreen where Leo Mercer stood rigidly, his boots planted squarely on the deck amidships as he gripped the handholds, features taut with concern. They'd suffered severe damage during the recent clash and were drifting in a damaged pattern that would carry them ever closer to the magnetar they'd only recently begun surveying.

Astrid stepped over, deliberately slowing her approach so as not to alarm him, careful to project solidity, reassurance. Mercifully, the ship still lurched sluggishly along its current course thanks to its residual thrust injectors. If luck held, they'd narrowly miss the blue giant's inferno before the Marauder finally succumbed to its deadly gravity. "Leo, I think—"

Before she could utter another word, the cruiser bucked and heaved so violently that both of them stumbled, crashing together harder than intended upon the decking plates. Astrid snatched a glimpse sideways past Leo; through the viewport, she witnessed the awful sight: the burgeoning flame of a megaflare erupting from the heart of the magnetar, a solar cataclysm hundreds of times more powerful than anything known to sustain human habitation or navigateable stellar bodies. That searing vortex of ionized plasma and X-rays would engulf worlds and incinerate everything within its path.

✦ ✦ ✦

Chapter 15: The Magnetar Flare
Scene 2: Tactical Dispute and Collision Course

Astrid righted herself by sheer force of will, using the momentum to pull Leo back into stability against the shuddering hull. His fingers clenched the nearby handrails as if the very fate of their battered ship depended on the strength of his grip— which wasn't entirely inaccurate.

"They're really going to throw all that raw energy out there?" Leo gasped, eyes wide with disbelief etched across his storm-gray face. Sweat glistened darkly on his furrowed brow in the dimmed cabin light. "Could this be..." He glanced around as if seeking reassurance from any material surface. 

"Incorrect," Astrid countered calmly through gritted teeth. "That ain't energy being 'thrown.' It's a colossal explosion of energy released as matter gets superheated in magnetic reconnection events." Her gaze transfixed the raging stormfront before them, an otherworldly aurora dancing on subatomic scales as countless tons of electromagnetic plasma charged toward oblivion. "The flare itself might last mere minutes but it'll scorch the light-years. We need to get this boat turned around pronto!"

"Why? So we can roast in the magnetar's outer corona like a pair of tardigrade toast, you mean?" Leaning to one side, Leo peered at the navigation display as it sketched out their spiraling trajectory with merciless precision. In mere hours, they would cross the event horizon into the star's belly if no course correction took place. Yet as desperate as their predicament seemed, neither option offered a pleasant outcome should their current vector persist.

"No way in hell should you let your own vessel become space junk by willingly diving headfirst into that furnace for nothing!" Leo insisted, hands balling into furious fists at his sides. "Think, damn it! Our mission was to survey. Not commit suicide!" Tension thrummed through each word uttered, a powder keg of pent-up frustration sparking just beneath his skin.

"How dare you question my judgment out of the blue, milksop," Astrid retorted bitterly, voice dripping disdain. She jabbed a calloused finger toward the maelstrom swirling before them. "This isn't some routine recon job anymore, not with that beast about to eat us whole! When pushed between the proverbial rock and fire, choices gotta be made." Bitterness coated every syllable and her stormy gaze bored into Leo like a drill bit scraping metal.

The bridge fell silent save for the mournful creaks and groans accompanying each tremor running through their beleaguered craft. Astrid kept her back arched defiantly, jaw set in stubborn resolve while Leo's features worked to process the harsh realities. It was clear these two seasoned warriors would have to reconcile vastly different philosophies if hope existed of salvaging themselves from this precarious predicament.

✦ ✦ ✦

The magnetar's pulsating core glowed incandescent blue-white against the abyssal black horizon, casting sickly illumination upon their terrified faces. 

Astrid's knuckles whitened as she gripped the shattered control yoke, her eyes wild and pleading to avoid collision while Leo's stolid expression belied the turmoil brewing behind the façade of military composure.

"Astrid, I'll admit what you've done so far has been...impulsive," Leo began carefully, "but pulling off a Hail Mary burn like this without thorough prep or checks puts both our lives needlessly on the line!"

"Don't pretend you have any better ideas, genius boy!" Astrid snapped back acidly, the name-calling barely masking desperate fear driving her actions. "We were dead in the water unless—"

"I've analyzed the approaching flux storm," interjected Leo hastily, cutting through the recrimination. "It'd consume us instantly. We simply don't have enough thrust to—"

"You think you know more?" Astrid interrupted again, voice quavering despite the bravado. "How can a relic from another century have any notion of facing this? This wasn't in the textbooks, Lieutenant!"

Leo bristled at the slight, his tone icy as he shot back, "Neither were the tech tricks you pulled getting us this far. We're an imperfect, mismatched duo trying to survive the uncharted expanse. Let's focus."

Their voices locked in heated deadlock as they hurtled closer to an unyielding destiny, stars streaking past like laser slashes across infinity. The blistering tempest grew exponentially more menacing, its tendrils lashing outward like vengeful tentacles seeking prey.

Suddenly, a spine-wrenching jolt slammed the command center. The Marauder lurched drunkenly side to side as multiple alarm klaxons screamed cacophonous warnings. Overwhelming scents of burning insulation and superheated fluids assaulted them simultaneously.

"We need an immediate fix or we—" began Astrid futilely as structural failures echoed outside. Debris peppered the bridge transparent dome, cracking it spider-web-pattern wise despite reinforcement spells.

"Now, Mercer!" she bellowed, pain-ringed eyes flashing with resolute determination.

Leo's hands flashed over console touchscreens as he initiated a priority override on key systems. The faint hum of compensators kicking online was a soothing counterpoint to the chaos around them. His brow furrowed intensely as he fought temporal distortions creeping in, the star eater's extreme gravitational influence warping spacetime itself.

Cyan displays lit up in urgent warning sequences yet still Leo pressed on, trusting his knowledge of orbital principles and the ship dynamics calculations racing within his computational mind. Sweat slickened the bridge floor as tremors intensified while he strained to recalibrate and reprioritize, one catastrophic failure too many spiking blood pressure to the brink of hypovolemic shock.

With a symphony of grinding servos, a hiss of pressurized hydraulic fluid, and a bone-jarring clunk, the crippled Marauder finally swung perpendicular to its death spiral trajectory, a single massive throttle venturi firing crimson-hot plasma into tiny nozzles spaced along the hull flanks. Centripetal force flattened Astrid into her seat as Leo grimaced through teeth ground white with tension, body straining forward toward the control console.

Outside, ionized plasma flames curled serpent-like from the retropropulsion vents, fighting valiantly to reverse momentum. For a stomach-churning infinity, the outcome hung uncertain, each second a ticking clock toward incineration by stellar winds and searing magnetar radiation.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo's fingers danced across tactile controls, eyes never leaving main displays where failing hull integrity flashed amber alongside climbing temperature gauges. Sweaty palms left slippery trails against synthetic grips as Astrid's curses echoed in his ear. "Pitiful, Mercer, just pitiful! The marauder's guts torn out like a freshly gutted targ at market!"

Her bitter tirade spurred him to focus tighter, pouring every ounce of years-killed skill into coaxing life-saving maneuver from wreckage of their once proud starship. Sweat, tears, and recaptured sanity dripped from Leo's chin as crimson fire vomited from the superheated thrusters. The Marauder groaned pitifully, protesting every attempt to right herself after her violent tumble into hellhole's gravity well. 

Outside, the battle-scarred hulk seemed to writhe under the onslaught of stellar winds screaming at hundreds of thousands of kilometers per hour, lashing with vicious energy until every inch of charred, heat-crumpled metal smoked and reeked of seared ferrocrete. Solar gusts howled with fury enough to pulverize any lesser vessel stone dead. And waiting like some eldritch celestial monstrosity, the magnetar's bloated mass pulsed ominously, poised to unleash wrath of untold mega-stocks upon those brave few who dared this abyss.

Slowly, agonizingly slowly, the Marauder responded to frantic efforts, struggling towards stability like a faltering drunken stag, each jolt sending a shockwave through the bucking bridge deck. Finally, the tortured hull began shifting sideways, away from the abyssal maw that had nearly swallowed them whole. 

Exhilarated relief surged though him but it would not last. Already the monitor lights flickered with new warning - they were not out of danger. At all. Rising in defiance from the depths were telltale wisps of stardust, coalescing rapidly into unmistakable form... 

An enemy fleet, far larger than their numbers led them to believe. And those ships bore no markings of legitimate traffic control nor enforcement. Instead they displayed garish finery that screamed plunder and piracy. Merciless black void ships bristling with weaponry, their angular profiles cutting through the void like razors driven by dark wills.

"Astrid, I make visual contact with unknown hostiles," Leo gasped aloud. "Confirmed pirate vessels. Six, possibly eight of them." Horror gripped his heart as he realized just how badly their chances now soured like unclean spirits on the worst night ever...

Astrid spared the barest glance from her intent scrutiny of damage readouts before fixing him with a look riddled with equal parts murderous rage and bleak despair. Only then did she deign to respond, voice dripping venom through gritted teeth. 

"...and you have the gall to inform me? Do I look fucking clueless, commander?" She hissed the final word like the venomous strike of a hungry viper, lean fingers drumming agitated patterns on the shattered console, tracing broken circuitry like caressing the corpse of a friend.

"Not so," Leo replied coolly, jaw clenched to hide the quake threatening to betray him. "I thought that given our precarious situation and near-dead status, your strategic preferences might alter."

He shifted slightly in his seat, ignoring the residual tingles from overexerted muscles screaming their protests anew as he continued steadily, tone even and measured despite racing heart beneath his ribs. 

"But the cold facts won't change even for my tactful suggestions. Our options are limited and the approaching pirates do us no favors."

# Chapter 16: Blind Navigation


The starfield beyond the damaged viewport spun a mad whirligig of light and shadow—Leo clung to the chair, stomach roiling as he watched the constellations blur past at horrific speed. Inertial compensators struggled valiantly but the g-force exerted by Marauder's desperate dive pressed mercilessly down upon his skull. Sweat beaded his forehead, eyes stinging from the relentless pressure. He blinked away the stars, focused exclusively on the faint holographic display projecting ship schematics and navigational data within the confines of his helmet.

Their battered vessel pirouetted within a hair's breadth of catastrophe, hurtling toward the unseen bulk of a magnetar—its gravitational well would quickly turn Marauder into a smoldering wreck. Yet the very gravity wave that threatened destruction also held the slim hope for escape. By embracing its embrace he could potentially slingshot around the ancient corpse and gain enough velocity to break free...

Provided they didn't collide first or the pirates decided to play grim reaper during what must surely be the longest, loneliest seconds of their lives. Leo's vision flickered around the edges, oxygen-rich air recirculated by the life support system tasting strange on his tongue. Each shallow breath expanded his chest, a constant reminder of the unforgiving atmosphere locked away behind the transparent, sealed dome of his envirosuit.

He risked a glance at Astrid, noting the captain's head tilted back against the cushions, her face slack and pale against the ruddy gleam of warning lights painting every surface in hellish hues. Even in this surreal freefall he remained perfectly composed, movements economical despite the obvious strain bearing down upon her like the weight of a collapsing skyscraper. Astrid was a force of nature personified—and it frightened Leo just how attuned he'd become to every subtle nuance of her presence, every ripple in an ocean far stranger than either of them had ever known.

Her eyes snapped open then, drilling into his as if she possessed psychic sight. Leo felt her probing gaze like a lance of pure energy searing into his very soul—a fleeting connection only possible after surviving such shared horrors together. "Navigation check," Astrid commanded in a flat monotone devoid of warmth, yet somehow more terrifying for its emotional detachment. Her hands moved across the battered console with practiced ease, bypassing damaged systems and hotwiring temporary workarounds as needed.

In mere minutes, her fingers danced across complex displays—the dim blue glow of holographs illuminating the rugged lines of her face like moonlight bathing in the depths of some otherworldly sea. "Estimating sixty-eight...sixty-nine...seventy seconds to event horizon insertion..." Astrid muttered, eyes never leaving the shifting calculations. "If current acceleration holds, we should begin feeling effects soon—" She trailed off abruptly, expression tightening into a grotesque parody of a smile that sent chills racing down Leo's spine.

Outside the ruined cockpit, an eerie purple haze swirled into existence on the curved metal shell—the telltale sign magnetar's gravitational influence began enveloping them whole. Involuntarily, Leo flinched at the sight—but maintained his focus, knowing any distraction could spell disaster. Already distortions rippled through local spacetime, the fabric of reality unraveling in visible waves.

"We've got company," he warned unnecessarily, thumb sliding across the comms interface built into his left glove. The response came immediately, each voice dripping with malice and anticipation: "Starlight Marauder— surrender yourself and maybe we let you live long enough for a proper interrogation..."

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo's hand froze on the comms control, muscles tensing as Astrid's gaze locked onto him from over her shoulder. Dark amusement danced in her eyes, tempered by a cold calculation his instincts couldn't decipher.

"Company?" she repeated mockingly, voice barely loud enough to cut through the hum filling the cabin. "How quaint." With a flick of her wrist, another interface lit up—the Marauder's weapons grids. "Looks like our maggot-brained friends have sent a little welcoming committee."

On the main display, mercifully shielded from direct line-of-sight, five mismatched vessels emerged from the swirling purple mists—the telltale signature of warp drive activation. Hulks of salvaged merchant vessels converted for piracy, sleek strike craft from forgotten colonial conflicts, even what appeared to be a repurposed mass driver cannon mounted onto a makeshift frigate. They danced around their prey in tantalizing maneuvers—a predator's chorus celebrating its imminent feast.

"Four heavy point-defense mounts," Leo murmured, running mental calculations. "Probably railguns, judging by the size. And those smaller craft—most likely swarmers, packing flechette volleys or directed EMP."

Astrid snorted, waving away his analysis. "All I care about right now is how much bang they can deliver before we dust 'em. Don't waste breath on tactical minutiae, soldier-boy."

Leo's hackles rose at the dismissive tone, years of ingrained discipline clashing against the brazen disregard for collateral damage displayed by these modern pirates. The chasm between his world view and Astrid's grew wider with each passing second, yet the thrill of the impending battle stirred his blood in ways he'd thought long extinguished—igniting a primal competitiveness that defied logic.

"We need a plan," he reminded her gruffly, struggling to rein in the adrenaline-fueled bravado threatening to override cooler judgment. Every fiber of his being screamed warning signals—that they were outnumbered, outgunned, and hopelessly entrenched in someone else's star system thanks to Astrid's reckless ambition. But pride would not permit defeat, not so close to achieving their goal.

Astrid rolled her shoulders, a fluid grace belying her unyielding resolve. "Plan? Feh—a waste o' time. Just prepare t'vearn some scars, because I ain't letting those scum take my ship without a fight."

Leo bit back the retort hovering on the tip of his tongue, realizing this was Astrid's core strength—and potentially her greatest weakness. Unwavering conviction and instinct had seen her through the unforgiving streets of the underworld, but the cosmos was different animal altogether. He recalled Kaelin's words on departure, how a lack of strategic depth might ultimately prove Astrid's downfall. Was he witnessing the seeds of that downfall in stark relief?

Before he could dwell further on such bleak musings, the bridge bucked once, twice, forcing him to clutch the nearest stanchion for balance. The inertial dampeners whined in protest as the Marauder surged forward again, chasing its unlikely gambit toward the event horizon.

Outside, warped star-space heaved and convulsed, reality itself trembling on the knife-edge between order and chaos. Gravity's fist tightened its relentless grip, energy surging through the bridge's hull like living lightning. The pirate crew screamed and clung to whatever bulkhead offered respite from the mounting tidal forces—except Astrid.

Stoic visage hardened into granite, she stood immobile, hands poised above auxiliary controls. Waiting. Watching. For something only she knew.

✦ ✦ ✦

The cloying reek of ozone scorched nostrils as solar flares danced in strobe-lit bursts across the viewport's darkened armor-glass. Spikes of crimson light seared retinas as starlight distorted through the swirling perturbations of spacetime.

"Time to earn those scars," Astrid growled, her voice a low rumble beneath the incessant groan of tortured metal and shrieking generators.

Leo gripped the edge of the command chair, knuckles white against the polished alloy as he struggled to suppress the roiling sensation of panic rising in his gut. Her unwavering resolve, forged in the crucible of the underworld's violence, both awed and terrified him. They were sailing into the heart of a maelstrom without a definitive plan or reliable backup—it was the very antithesis of anything his military training or even his years flight-testing advanced fighter prototypes had prepared him for.

As if reading his thoughts, Astrid's gaze caught and held his, piercing depths in a moment of unspoken understanding. For an instant, the hellish turmoil around them dropped away, and it was just the two of them locked in an orbit of anticipation and trepidation. Then, the Marauder lurched again, throwing him off-balance as the inertial compensators fought to maintain a semblance of equilibrium in the face of the encroaching singularity. 

"Astrid!" he bellowed over the cacophony, straining to be heard. "Give me—

Silenced by the crashing boom of a thunderously loud alarm, their exchange disintegrated into fragmented gestures as they each scrambled to diagnose the new threat threatening their precarious stability. Critical systems flashed red and amber as automated warnings filled the air like a thousand screaming ravens:

"Cooling failure, Deck 4! Decompression imminent!"

"Hull breach, Frame 37! Sealing initiates NOW!"

"Momentum dump system offline!"

Leo frantically tapped at the main console, fingers dancing across a keyboard where keys shuddered from the impact of pounding vibration. His heart slammed in his chest as the abyssal math of propulsion and maneuvering scrolled past in a dizzying blur, the calculations screaming impossible odds. Even his prodigious skillset couldn't reconcile this mess fast enough to chart a successful egress. Panic clawed at his throat, demanding answers to questions no one could possibly provide in time...

Then, Astrid moved, fluid grace belied by the raw power coiled within her limbs. She planted her palms atop the commander's station, fingers tapping out a command sequence so rapid even his trained eyes could barely track its frenetic arc.

"No brakes," she declared, features pinched in concentration. "No thrusters either. We dive, baby. Burn till we can't... then hope our shielding holds."

"What?" Horror colored the single word as comprehension bloomed, cold dread spreading from gut to bones as realization crashed down upon him. This was reckless bordering on suicidal—a desperate bid to outrun the unstoppable maw of an eater-hole without propulsion or adequate protection. Yet even as terror coiled its icy fangs around every coherent thought, Leo saw the logic behind her decision—perhaps the sole avenue open to them given the dire state of their crippled vessel. It was mad, but he grasped its audacity. More than that, a twisted echo of Astrid's steely resolve began to resonate within him...

Beneath quaking deckplates—boards etched with age and grime that would have sparked derision from any seasoned spacer Leo had crossed paths with—a low thrum built, building pressure and heat until the bridge became a furnace box.

✦ ✦ ✦

The vortex swallowed them whole. 

A singular point of infinity, an abyss unutterably vast, opened its maw and engulfed Starlight Marauder. One moment they plunged headlong into darkness, next they were racing through the heart of creation itself.

Light-years contracted to inches, the cosmos compressing into an immersive hologram wrapping around the stricken ship. Streaks of luminescence flared past the viewport like brushstrokes across a celestial canvas - supernovae, nebulae, blazing black holes. Distant galaxies tumbled, whirled and careened by in dizzying profusion while the very fabric of spacetime undulated like an ethereal tide.

Inside the vessel, Astrid fought gravity to keep her footing as the hull groaned under unprecedented stresses. Every strut and beam sang a symphony of protest, deck plates shuddering violently enough to rip handholds from the walls. Alarms screamed in cacophonous discord, status boards bathing the bridge in a strobing nightmare of red and yellow.

Leo clung to his seat, vision locking to the aft screen as if mesmerized by an apocalyptic ballet unfolding outside. Marauder's engines cast a searing glare across the void, ion plasma trails streaming away from her drive mounts like spectral comet tails. Heat shields flared orange, glowing like embers beneath siege-fire assault, while inertial dampeners hissed on overdrive to stave off the lethal g-forces shredding systems and crew alike.

Around them, the universe imploded into chaotic glory - stars bursting, worlds colliding, quantum fluctuations sparking forth like fireflies in the void. Time lost meaning, seconds stretching to eternity and back again as they hurtled onwards in relativistic torment. A silent, deafening scream echoed in Leo's mind as his world narrowed to the blistering engines and the warrior woman riding shotgun to madness.

Then, star-bright, leviathan-shaped monstrosity loomed ahead. Astrid jolted upright at the sudden contact alert, eyes snapping to the forward sensors. Heart thudding in her chest, she watched as the monstrous apparition filled the viewports - the hulking form of some ancient derelict drifting lazily across the path of their doomed plunge.

"What?" Leo gasped beside her, incredulous and horrified as behemoth ruins swelled to fill the field of view. Asteroid-forged bulkheads, labyrinths of conduits and driveshells, great halls and chambers festively strewn with relics beyond counting and ken.

"Hold on..." Astrid breathed, reaching for the master control yoke. With no other escape, no last resort left undone Marauder's final collision course was the only option remaining.

"Astrid--" Leo protested weakly as she punched in the settings. The helm trembled in her grasp as she angled for interception.

"Too close," she whispered to herself, calculating odds that would leave a bookmaking asteroid miner queasy with doubt. The dying cruiser plowed onward as if hell-bent on transpiration into that alien hull. 

Impact was inevitable. And even the Star-Eater's titanic corpse might not survive the encounter.

# Chapter 17: Casualties of the Void

They were a single bad impulse away from oblivion, hurtling towards the waiting behemoth at point-blank range - two insignificant flecks of stardust against the massive hull looming large in the viewscreen. Heat shields already strained redline, overloaded thrusters groaning under impossible stresses as Captain Astrid Ross wrestled the crippled Marauder onto a collision course.

Leo gripped the edge of his acceleration couch, jaw clenched white as he braced against the violent pitch and yaw. This couldn't possibly end well. Not even close. "Astrid, what the fuck?!" he yelled over the cacophony of wailing alarms and tortured metal. "We're going to splat ourselves against that thing!"

The pirate captain's reply was grim, her focus laser-sharp on lining up the strike. "No choice anymore. We either get swallowed whole, spread across light-years to decorate some long-dead galactic sphincter - or make this bastard our own personal hole."

"You've gone insane," Leo spat, voice cracking despite himself as star-stuff turned to furnace heat painting the bow viewports a molten crimson. 

The impact came as one, a tremendous shockwave rippling back though hull plates and skeletal supports, throwing crew into wild tangos - bruised backs slamming against consoles, loose cargo shifting madly in zero-g chaos.

Through the storm of disorientation, Astrid clung tenaciously to her command seat, riding out brutal oscillations triggered by glancing hits. Main drives howled their death agonies then faded abruptly as primary fuel injectors ruptured outward in a shower of sparks. Emergency power kept them from total darkness but barely. Dim red lights cast eerie shadows as decks groaned and shifted ominously beneath their feet.

Leo struggled to climb free amidst the wreckage scattered across the bridge, hauling himself over broken equipment until he stumbled to his knees by Astrid's side. She'd slumped forward, arms draped limply over the tactical station, hair plastered to her skull in sweat and grime.

"Vex," Leo breathed, gently pulling her upright to meet his concerned gaze. Her eyes were unfocused, staring into something only she could see.

"Gotta...move," she mumbled, shaking off his touch with sudden ferocity. "Before-"

A dull rumble thrummed through the hull plates, low but intensifying. Astrid cut off with a wince, squinting wearily at flickering sensor data. Even as crew reports trickled in, most comms knocked out or jammed, the gravity of their situation became gut-wrenchingly clear: they had indeed smashed themselves halfway into the derelict's rusting, pitted flank. And that ruddy beast of old ships didn't seem pleased.

"We're pinned," Astrid said bluntly, voice numb with defeat and dread. "No getting out unless that hull gives way...and I'd rather eat my boots than count on the whims of some ancient wreck." She took a slow breath, visibly fighting down the urge to start screaming. "Cargo bay's probably the only place to try and patch ourselves up. If we play our cards right, might just live long enough for the ESO to find us..."

Leo looked at Astrid in disbelief. They were stranded in a hostile metal tomb, bleeding air and coolant by the minute. "Yeah...because nothing says peaceful rescue like a panicked evacuation from a hulk teetering on planetary-scale destruction."

"Just shut up and follow me," Astrid snapped, already unclipping from her chair and stumbling toward the descending lift tunnel.

✦ ✦ ✦

Astrid staggered through the darkening corridors, her boots scraping against torn deckplates. Every step sent jarring pain lancing up her leg where shards of ceramic armor had bitten deep into flesh and muscle. It felt like walking through a frozen nightmare.

Mercer limped alongside her, jaw clenched tight as he clutched his side. Blood seeped slowly between his gloved fingers, leaving crimson smears on his environment suit. With each labored exhale, he winced, face paler than before under the emergency lighting.

The eerie silence within the battered Starlight Marauder was broken only by the soft whirrs of damaged systems and their ragged breathing. Panic threatened to boil over, but Astrid kept it leashed, forcing herself to focus. 

They needed to reach the cargo bay without delay – the ship's heart still pumped life-support air into the main sections, at least for now. But every second bought them precious room to maneuver if the hull cracked open or worse.

"You okay?" Astrid asked gruffly, not expecting a sincere reply. Her hand shot out to steady Leo as he swayed on his feet.

"Just peachy," he gurgled bitterly, eyes squeezing shut against the pain. "Getting reacquainted with my ex-wife, she's been trying to kill me for weeks now..."

Astrid snorted. A thin rim of ice encased her bruised heart, but beneath there remained a spark – maybe fondness, maybe something more. Could never tell anymore. All that mattered was the next few vital minutes as they fought for their lives against the relentless void.

Together they stumbled onward until reaching the cargo bay. A haze of cooling vapor hung heavy, mingling with the acrid reek of scorched wiring. Three grav tethers dangled inert near an overturned crate, discarded by hurried escapees probably.

"Grab those," Astrid ordered curtly, dragging herself toward the battered medbay setup near the bulkhead. Medkits, bandages, and antiseptic wipes were scattered about, mostly undamaged – yet another testament to a harrowed crew struggling to keep their ghost ship operational.

Within the cramped confines of the tiny infirmary, Astrid began applying pressure dressings and running diagnostics on the wounded duo. Merciless medical AI chirped at her to sedate Mercer, claiming he likely suffered internal bleeding, but she refused – wouldn't risk the pain numbing his reflexes when they needed him alert.  

Leo grimaced through gritted teeth watching Astrid work, wondering how someone so tough could hide such deft hands under her calloused exterior. He forced himself to focus instead on their dismal situation.

"So what's the plan, Captain Pirate?" he croaked around a sudden spasm of agony in his abdomen. "Let's hear your illustrious strategy for getting out alive..."

Astrid froze mid-bandage, eyes narrowing. "Oh, it's simple really. We've got maybe an hour tops until this scrapheap implodes or the leak drains our air completely – either way, game over. So our choices are limited to finding something to weld a breach with, ripping apart furniture to reinforce weak points, or—"

"Pretend to send out a distress signal to lure in rescuers while playing dead in stasis pods?"

"Yeah, well, that wasn't in my original plans. Let's just say the circumstances have become rather...unprecedented." Astrid's lips twisted wryly. "How's your stomach holding up? You look like you could vomit up all the lead weights strapped to your ankles."

Leo waved away concern, glaring.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo's gaze lingered on Astrid, captivated by the ruthless gleam in her eyes, the firm set of her mouth as she detailed their dire situation. His stomach churned queasily, acid burning his throat, but he forced down bile, swallowing the bitter taste of defeat alongside recriminations for letting things spiral so perilously out of control.

"I'm fine," he growled, hating how brittle his voice sounded, the underlying trembling he couldn't quite mask. "Not exactly feeling festive, but we've got bigger problems than my gut right now." Astrid flicked her silver-flecked bangs back, meeting his fierce glare with one of her own. "I'd argue that's an understatement," she snapped, fingers drumming a rapid tattoo against her thigh. 

Leo followed her agitated motion with his eyes, drawn inexorably to touch that sinewy muscle, imagine trailing kisses along its corded length. He jerked his gaze upward, face heating, only to collide with Astrid's piercing violet stare, the intensity nearly bowling him over again. What was happening to him?

A knock at the bulkhead disrupted the charged atmosphere, jolting them both back to reality. "Ship systems are experiencing catastrophic failures across the board!" The panicked cry of Helm Officer Dax came muffled through reinforced metal, underscored by ominous groans and screeches. 

"Heat exchangers offline, cooling coils ruptured––" Astrid cut him off, already moving towards the door. "Mercer, keep working on that patch – you're closer to the hull breach. I'll assess the damage control stations and see if any salvageable parts can be rerouted." Her tone brooked no argument as she ripped open the seal, plunging into the fray beyond.

Leo bit back a snarl, not liking being left behind while Astrid charged headlong into chaos, but knew better than to second-guess her in crisis mode. With a sigh rough with despair, he hauled himself upright, limbs heavy and uncoordinated, and turned his attention back to the stubborn seam girdling airlock three. Sweat-soaked hair clung to his skull, his shirt soaked through with perspiration, clinging revealingly to his lean torso—but none of that mattered compared to the countdown ticking away in his mind...

*50 minutes remaining*

Grasping wrench after wrench, Leo wielded brute force, channeling adrenaline into every blow as he battled the obstinate chunk of warped aluminum. If he didn't crack it open soon, they were both dead men walking. Suddenly, hot pain seared his thumb, and merciful darkness blossomed at the edges of his vision. Clutching the wounded digit, Leo struggled to maintain a grip with his other hand as spots danced before his eyes...

Just then, Astrid burst back in, visor retracted, face etched with frustration. She paused upon spotting Leo, hovering precipitously near blackout, and hurried to him with a curse. "For fuck's sake, Mercer! Are you intentionally pushing yourself too far?" In the distance, the hull shuddered ominously beneath starlit blackness.

"I think he passed out a few seconds ago," Astrid shouted to Dax over her shoulder, catching Leo halfway as he started to slump. Strapping a flexible first-aid pad around his throbbing thumb, she hoisted him effortlessly, muscles rippling beneath her flight suit as she swung him upside-down by his feet. 

"You might be right about heading to medbay anyway," Dax panted in response, frantically fiddling with readouts.

✦ ✦ ✦

Chapter 17 – Casualties of the Void, Scene 4

Astrid whirled Leo’s dangling form around, her breath misting the viewport as an unobstructed vista of stardust sprawled beyond the ship's ragged puncture wound. Against the inky velvet expanse, brilliant spirals of aurora borealis laced through the void - ionization trails etched by nearby supernovae or perhaps the Marauder's own superheated plasma from the recent close call. A shiver ran down Astrid's spine, even as concern for her unlikely companion took precedence.

“Wake up, Leo,” she growled close to his maskless face, shaking him lightly. His unfocused gaze drifted slowly upward, bleary violet eyes gradually focusing on hers. Astrid kept her expression stern, not wanting sympathy to undermine his already precarious mental state if he sensed any softness.

After a tense moment, Leo blinked several times and swallowed dryly. “Did I... pass out again?” he rasped, voice hoarse from breathing thin atmos. He glanced past Astrid at the glittering celestial view and sucked in a sharp breath, struggling to stand upright.

The faint hum of a proximity alert caught Astrid off guard, her attention suddenly split between Leo relearning gravity at an alarming rate and rapidly approaching unknown contacts. She snagged his arm just as he stumbled, steadying him as she scanned the tactical display. The ship's perimeter was flaring red - masses of smaller vessels swarming, cutting off escape routes with menacing precision.

Leo’s foggy eyes snapped into focus as he struggled for balance against her firm grip. “Is that… a fleet? Did we trigger some kind of trap?”

Astrid squeezed out a tight-lipped smile, pride mingling with her fear for them both. "Not entirely your fault this time." She spared a look over her shoulder, nodding curtly at Dax's frantic efforts to analyze their predicament. With no clear shields left intact, the pirated data terminals had become an instant death sentence once hacked. "Let's hope our clever tricks hold up against pursuit." Turning fully back to Leo, she lifted an eyebrow critically as he wobbled but resisted falling. "Looks like you get another taste of the Marauder's acceleration – we need to shift course, fast. Medbay will have to wait if our pursuers catch us."

At her warning, Leo stiffened, teeth gritted. Something flickered behind his eyes – determination rather than defeat. He met Astrid's calculating stare, and together their gazes flicked to the swirling vortex outside. Within its shimmering heart resided a tantalizing secret only a madwoman would chase...

And he just might give in to the temptation.

# Chapter 18: Vows in the Dark


Darkness swallowed them whole as Astrid yanked the controls savagely starboard, sending the Starlight Marauder careening past a scorched moon fragment. Leo grunted, crashing back into his seat as the inertial damping struggled to compensate for the rapid slew. Recycled oxygen hissed through the hull – a hollow, metallic sound, punctuated by the rattling stress of strained alloys.

"Brace for—"

But Astrid cut herself short as the warning trembled in her throat unspoken. This close, the fleet gave no grace period before opening fire, their beams stabbing across intervening void with millisecond timing that belied how desperately these hunters sought their prey. A flare of orange-white seared the cockpit windows, spalling shattered fragments onto the command deck with screeching velocity.

"Hold on!" Astrid snarled, hauling the ship through a dizzying series of evasive twists meant to confound guidance systems – not intended to soothe their riders. The G forces flattened Leo against the harness, sweat beading on his brow as he clung to whatever handhold presented itself, barely recognizing the burning latticework of stars through the flickering warnings.

"Leo, check our status," Astrid barked over the cacophony, voice steady despite the chaos. Her hands danced across the command board, patching together damaged conduits under the screaming din of stressed circuits. Somewhere beneath the roar, a crack echoed through the decking, a ominous harbinger of impending failure.

Mercer fought free of his binding webbing, eyes blazing with desperate determination as he pried himself loose from the inertia constraints. Flailing through the turbulent heat of the cockpit, his numb fingers finally found purchase on a console, dragging himself forward to slump beside Astrid at the helm.

"Life Support yellow. Sensors half-functional," Mercer gasped, fighting to breathe against the pressure exerting on his chest plates. Hot rivulets of moisture trickled down his forehead, stinging where cold metal scraped his skin. The acrid tang of superheated plastics and plasma burn seared his nostrils, mixing grotesquely with the sterile musk of emergency oxygen.

Outside, sparks danced wildly as more hits struck home, painting the Starlight Marauder with a hellish corona. Heat shielding glowed an incandescent white before venting in great, explosive whuffs, leaving streaks of black carbonaceous debris trailing from marring plates.

"We're taking too much damage. We can't keep this up," Mercer warned urgently. Astrid bit her lip, considering options rendered treacherous by dwindling resources – or faith in those already spent. Panic threatened to rear its head but she tamped it ruthlessly down, focusing instead on the singular fact anchoring her: Leo Mercer was still by her side.

"It'll have to do," she spat, a hair's breadth from growling those words past clenched teeth. Her gaze fell upon his battered features, face set in lines of grim resolve. Perhaps that was what sealed their fates – their similarities.

Rising gracefully despite the relentless pounding, Astrid moved to stand beside her reluctant co-pilot, reaching out to cup bruised knuckles in her palm. Beneath her touch, Leo's calloused flesh prickled with cool sweat trapped between layers of spacesuit fabric, smearing droplets thinly across her own dry skin in a fleeting moment of tender contact.

"I know what I want," Astrid breathed.

✦ ✦ ✦

Chapter 18: Vows in the Dark

Beneath scarlet alerts flashing on bulkheads and screens, the Marauder creaked in protest around them – an ominous symphony heralding the starship's mortal fragility. 

"Damn it," Leo snarled over suit comms, craning his neck to peer aft at where the infernal craft once dwelled, now shredded in ruin against vacuum. His eyes narrowed to slits behind glare-resistant optics as he grappled with Astrid's assertion, her voice echoing tinnily within close quarters. How could one man possibly survive such cataclysm?

"We... we didn't kill him," Mercer reiterated stubbornly, jaw flexing with renewed determination under Astrid's unyielding scrutiny.

"Not yet," the pirates retorted wryly, a thread of malice lacing her tone.

"And if they retrieve you—"

"Too late for maybes." Astrid waved off Leo's concerns dismissively with a flick of pale fingers, sending an errant strand of silver-streaked hair dancing against her cheek. She leaned closer, until only a whisper separated their helmets – a futile barrier against the intimate tumult brewing.

"If their tech doesn't vaporize me on the spot, your people will definitely make the trade a necessity," Astrid whispered hoarsely, drawing a rough line through Leo's rigid spine with the tips of her gloves.

He swallowed audibly, face paling perceptibly beneath his reflective visor. Astrid watched the play of conflicting emotions cross his angular features – the stubborn loyalty, the practical acknowledgment, the primal unease. All perfectly natural. In another universe, far removed from the toxic alliance currently binding them...

The pirate woman shifted restlessly, armor creaking soft protests. "A promise ain't worth two huffed creds without a way to back it up, no matter who gives it."

Leo bristled, an eddy of rankled pride surfacing amidst cracks splitting his stoic facade. For a microsecond, she glimpsed the old military commander, ever quick to dispute and right perceived wrongs, even in the most bizarre extremity of events.

Her smirk twitched – yes, precisely the reaction she'd aimed for.

"We're dead men walking, Mercer. At least among our own lot." Her lips, thin and colorless despite the rich red hue of the suit's environment control, curved wickedly above the gold accents framing her irises. Those predatory orbs seemed to glow more luminously in the dim light streaming down from Marauder's ports: an eerie testament to her ferocious vitality. "Don't pretend like there aren't consequences if word of this partnership bleeds into other circles. Reputation precedes loyalty every damned time."

A muscle in Leonardo's cheek pulsed once, twice – then stilled as cool acceptance flooded slowly behind his eyes. The realization settling over him felt curiously similar to the first taste of space's unforgiving gravity, a force so pervasive, it molded a man even in repose until every cell acknowledged its presence. He was done arguing tooth and nail, convinced Astrid would see reason... because she didn't have a choice.

Leo lifted one gloved hand, extended finger by finger. At each point of contact, icy synthetic material adhered with a faint hiss to Astrid's, bonding them at wrists. When finally their palms pressed together, a jolt of static electricity snapped through the link, sparking tiny arcs of blue-white fire.

"You're buying me time."

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo held fast to Astrid as the Starlight Marauder lurch-shuddered through sudden evasive maneuvers. Alarms screeched, cacophonous white noise assaulting their eardrums via vibro-hearing units since the void itself offered no ulterior soundscape for cover. In the chaos, Mercer found momentary solace within the sheer muscularity of Vex's suited form, locked close at the chest and interlaced arms. The temperature-sensitive fabric clung dampily to exposed skin where their linked hands and forearms rested against the black leather flight suits, exuding the combined tang of antiseptic wipes, the sharpness of Astrid's citrus-spice perfume, and Mercer's own salt-sweat undertone.

"Pyraxi fighters," Astrid ground out, golden-eyed stare narrowing to slits as targeting systems pinged alerts across her HUD. "Four of the bastards closing fast off port quarter. Shields can absorb the initial salvo but—"

"Marauder can't outrun them in short-term," Leo finished grimly, mental calculations already racing through probable scenarios. His index finger twitched against the reinforced webbing of Vex's suit – searching for thrum, feeling for metal-to-metal contact anywhere along their sealed union. "We need to—

"Squirt one, two, three!" Astrid barked orders that sent the Marauder careening sharply starboard while launching targeted missile salvos from concealed weapon arrays. Laser turrets whined up to life, spitting forth lances of charged plasma designed to vaporize armor plating and seek life signatures. The pirate captain's free wrist darted to her comms panel, fingers flying across the holo-keys as she routed sensor feeds to auxiliary stations hidden in the ship's cargo holds and engineering compartments, hoping to keep Pyraxi trackers guessing about Marauder's true configuration.

Asteroid fragments and molten debris from previous dogfights swirled chaotically around the battling vessels, some close enough to clip at empty suitskins or rattle cabin walls but mostly keeping a perilous distance to avoid catastrophic damage. Dust motes danced within the faint illumination leaking through the damaged main shield, suspended in microgravity until attracted by ambient electrostatic charges. Vex's lips skated back in a vicious snarl before she bit them shut, jaw muscles bulging beneath mottled grays and blacks.

"Mercer, I'm starting my turn–wait..."

A lurching shimmy knocked Marauder sideways as something massive impacted her stern bulkhead near the docking bays, sending shockwaves rolling through every piece of the vessel – jarring, bone-juddering, and nauseatingly prolonged. A strangled hiss escaped Vex as if punched in the gut. The hit had ruptured internal airlocks and equalized pressure too quickly throughout decks one through six, making any area prone to decompression.

Astrid slapped the comms unit again, snarling what could have been an oath or encouragement into microphone mesh as she frantically rebalanced maneuvering thrusters, struggling to align sensors with the nearest exit tunnel of Kaldorian-controlled asteroid belt as Pyraxi fighters continued to press their attack unrelentingly. Their relentless pursuit made sense – corner Marauder in open space outside planetary or station defenses, and finishing the raid became merely a matter of timing their final assault. No room for retreat, only elimination.

"Acknowledged," Leo managed hoarsely into the comms after several attempts to steady himself against Vex's substantial frame without disengaging hand-to-hand, fighting the urge to cling wildly even though they.

✦ ✦ ✦

Adrenaline-sour saliva stung the corners of Vex's mouth, taste buds scorched by the caustic mix of fear, loathing, and desperate concentration coursing through her veins like liquid fire. She strained against the seat restraints, gritting teeth as Pyraxi beam-lances sliced scorch marks across Marauder's port bow while ion thrusters stuttered futilely against pursuit. Sweat trickled down her neck to soak the collar of her flight suit despite zero-G conditions.

"...fighting it," Leo gasped out, his breath hot against the side of Vex's neck. His arms tightened around her waist reflexively when another shockwave ripped through the ship, making his bones rattle. He clapped hands over her ears as if that futile gesture might protect them both from the screaming stress vibrations threatening to crack ship hull alike from within. 

The sudden crunch of metal snapping sent pangs shooting up Leo's forearms searing into his hands at the exact moment he hunched forward, shielding her head against the shattering explosion of a Pyraxi fighter's engines starboard. Vomiting in microgravity left him dizzy and weak as the reek of char and ozone filled his lungs. 

Gasping, retching, he struggled blindly for purchase among torn cables, spilled controls, and splintered console components...and slammed into a wall, a jagged edge scraping a bleeding gash above his brow. Stunned but still clinging obstinately to Vex, his heart pounded in his ears almost loud enough to drown out the creaks of strained frame and groans of stressed metal working to absorb the punishment dealt them. His vision blurred red at the edges as a rivulet of blood ran down past his eye, leaving a salty, warm trail.

He wanted - needed - to look up at the sky, to see how much farther they would be dragged under the gunsights of enemies before Kaldorians finally delivered them a lifeline. But couldn't tear gaze away from her profile as it ghosted past, pale blue eyes haunted as ghostly shadows reflected the crimson emergency lighting. In this frozen slice of time suspended between battle and death, the war between mercenary and soldier faded into insignificance next to the raw fear of the abyss yawning darkly ahead.

The ship gave a long lamentable groan as a section of deckplates lifted underfoot like ice shelves in meltdown - Marauder's main propulsion systems dying agonizing deaths, spilling their guts in glowing chunks of ablative insulation and superheated hydrazine fuel amidst the carnage. Alarms screamed for attention, flashing lights strobing in pulsing rhythms that drove through pain to reach that most primal of senses - hearing.

"Leo?" Vex breathed against his lips, voice as hollow as a child's toy telephone after static clearance. For an age, there was only the hissing of life support air recycling, the wet chug of external thermal radiators shedding heat, and the eternal sigh of space cold embracing their damaged craft like a lover. Then, faint, a distant rumble. Thunder muted by distance and the oppressive vacuum.

Astrid slowly released the comms microphone, letting it droop heavy toward the buckled floor plates. She turned her face into the crook of Leo's neck, lips brushing his skin as if seeking some shred of vital warmth in their frozen hell amidst the shattered deck ruins and burning shreds of Pyraxi debris trailing behind the crippled Starlight Marauder.
