# Chapter 11: Blackout at Sector 7

Chapter 11: Blackout at Sector 7

Leo materialized in the dimly glowing bridge, straining against inertial dampeners designed to prevent even the slightest motion during hyperspace jumps. He landed heavily amidst the low hum of systems powering back up, disoriented by the sudden shift to conventional propulsion. The Marauder eased into its sleek profile, gleaming alloys painted pitch black under the artificial illumination of instrument panels and control interfaces.

"It's like a tomb in here," Astrid muttered from where she gripped the pilot's seat. Her gloved hand cradled the disruptor pistol holstered across her knee, ready to unleash kinetic death if need be. The air felt heavy, recycled and slightly stale, a reminder that the Starlight's exterior shell was breached. A faint tang of ozone mingled with the coppery scent of spilled blood—and his own sweat, the telltale clamminess not entirely due to the lingering microgravity. His heart pounded in anticipation of the unknown dangers lying ahead.

"Alright, let's check the situation," Leo said over the intercom as he slid into the copilot's chair. His fingers danced nimbly across the holographic controls springing to life before him. He winced when the nav display revealed their location—a godforsaken pocket of space on the rim of inhabited zones. Just where Orlo had promised them the data relay would be hiding in plain sight. "Looks like our friend made good on that threat."

On nearby monitors, grainy feeds showed armed patrols closing in on the Marauder from multiple angles—their sleek craft adorned with crimson Imperial eagles. Merciless starboard-facing laser cannons winked open along the freighter's flanks in preparation for intercept.

"Too much firepower to outrun outright," Astrid agreed grimly. "Better make peace with the prospect of an intimate dance with our adversaries." She tapped commands into the main screen, bringing external cameras online. Thermal signatures blazed across the void like distant suns as the patrol ships opened fire on range, ion blasts churning the darkness and sending fragments of melted metal spinning away from burning hulks.

"Helluva welcome party," Leo grumbled, eyeing the devastation unfold on screen. Unshielded hull plating couldn't resist the onslaught, seams splitting open under relentless barrage—hollow echoes of tortured metal as their opponents tore the Marauder apart. "EMP must've fried most of our comm gear, too. Can't raise anyone on the station or sector wide net." No way to hail for backup, stranded alone amongst hostile craft... This really was just him, Vex, and whoever else still drew breath onboard against overwhelming odds. A pit formed in his stomach as the tactical display updated to show three cruisers and half a dozen fighters pincer-maneuvering to surround and cut off any potential escape.

Astrid bit back a curse while scanning navigation options, her face a mask of serene focus betrayed only by the tight white line of her lips and the slight flex of clenched fists against thighs. Sweat trickled down the sides of her face, evaporating instantly in the chilled confines. When she finally spoke, her voice carried the calm, controlled edge of battle-hardened veterans everywhere: "All right, we'll improvise."

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo leaned forward in his command seat, hands clasped behind his head as he studied the tactical map scrolling across the main viewer. The situation was grim – five heavy cruisers and eight fighter interceptors moving in to hem them in. All it would take was one lucky hit to cripple the Marauder.

"Astrid, we need to-" His words caught in his throat as the pirate commander suddenly launched herself across the width of the cockpit, slamming a cylindrical object into a port nestled just above the control arrays. A shower of sparks erupted from the panel as she crouched over it with fierce intensity. Even without touching, Leo could feel the deck reverberate from the impact.

"What the devil was that?" he asked, genuine disbelief dripping from each word. The last he'd seen, they were running blind after taking severe damage from hostile fire.

Astrid straightened up, wiping sweat from her brow with the sleeve of her tactical jacket. Her dark hair stuck out wildly in every direction from a crash helmet she'd somehow neglected.

"Hacking equipment you so thoughtfully provided. Trying to bring up some functioning comms." She scowled, tapping a gloved finger against another console. "Shame about those patrol boats cutting our external antennae, eh? Made my job rather more difficult."

Leo blinked rapidly, struggling to reconcile her casual nonchalance with the adrenaline-pumping chaos unfolding outside. They were literally under attack and this woman seemed almost amused by her own technical acrobatics.

"You have a very... unconventional coping mechanism," he managed to say. "Isn't there something called 'remaining calm under pressure' back where you're from? Because if I didn't know better, I'd think you just enjoyed seeing our ship tear itself to pieces to spite me."

That earned him raised eyebrows and an incredulous snort from Astrid. "Oh please, Commander Mercer. Let's cut the cute routine, shall we? You aren't exactly Mr. Chill yourself, despite that rosy-cheeked 'ooh what a fine mess we're in' act you pulled aboard." She cocked her hip and fixed him with an unsettlingly level stare, arms crossed over her chest. "We both know your heart's racing about as fast as mine and yours isn't exactly concealed under several inches of armor-plated muscle."

Leo felt his cheeks flush hot at that pointed assessment. When had she gotten so perceptive in just a handful of days'? He shifted uncomfortably under her gaze before settling on a defiant grin, deciding to call her bluff.

"Oh don't give me credit for introspection I clearly don't possess. You seem fixated on getting under people's skin today." He waved around at the shattered viewports and flickering systems warning screens. "Care to tell me how much longer we can keep playing this game before someone actually bites the big one? Preferably not us, given you seem to prefer us alive for reasons unknown."

"I like a good challenge," Astrid retorted simply, meeting his impish smile with equal arrogance. "Besides," she added, her tone turning speculative, "seems like you're adapting quickly enough considering you started out so far removed from everything I do for a living."

Despite himself, Leo found his annoyance simmering closer to fascination as Astrid's enigmatic presence filled the small command room. There was something captivating about the pirate's unflappable confidence bordering on recklessness.

"Just how long have you been out here pirating in interstellar no man's land, anyway?" he posed aloud, genuinely curious now. Any normal human being would've fallen apart months ago facing threats like these on a daily basis.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo's challenging question hung heavy in the thin air of the command chamber, echoing slightly off its metal walls lined with circuitboards and control consoles in disarray from yet another chaotic system failure. Yet as Astrid absorbed his probing scrutiny through hooded eyes, those eerie irises seemed to swirl with stardust rather than betray any sign of unease.

"A century and change by your measurement," she replied calmly, her voice muffled slightly by the respirator mask clutched tightly to her face as wisps of cold, acrid smoke wafted from the vent ducts high overhead. She leaned back into her chair now, stretching the taut leather of her flight suit across corded muscles barely covered by her singed cape.

"Time travels different out in the expanse where stars birth worlds anew each moment," Astrid continued, gazing upwards towards the darkened main viewport, its fragmented remains allowing splinters of sector light to bleed crimson against the inky blackness beyond the wrecked hull plating.

"Moon cycles, market prices of xenon fuel... even personal lifespans can span generations depending on which side of a wormhole jump you find yourself while crossing realities."

Her words painted an awe-inspiring, unfathomable tapestry of lives lived beyond the scope of Earth's limited understanding, civilizations born, thrived and crumbled among the swirling chaos of interstellar frontier.

"You adapted remarkably fast considering," Astrid remarked, shifting her gaze back down to meet Leo's startled stare. Her features softened infinitesimally beneath the harsh glow of the emergency lighting—something akin to genuine admiration glimmered within the depths of those otherworldly eyes.

"You humans may be slow to evolve, but you have remarkable tenacity once prodded. Quite the contrast from my kin..." She let that last observation trail off on a thoughtful whisper, almost to herself before focusing sharply back on him.

"Flying ships is more than just muscle memory and brute reaction, Commander. It takes intellect, cunning, intuition—and knowing when someone's full attention isn't solely on the controls, not just in critical engagements." With a deft motion, Asterid tossed aside the shattered remnants of the comms headset that had once kept them linked with their stranded comrades. Its brittle plastics cracked and spun lazily amidst the growing drift of flakes and scraps.

In a heart-wrenching gesture of solidarity, she pulled off her own oxygen mask then carefully placed it in his waiting hand. Then again with deliberate, measured slowness, Astrid unlaced and shrugged free her respirator as well, exhaling heavily as if finally breathing the pure, thin vacuum of liberated freedom.

The faintest blush touched both cheeks beneath weathered faces half-obscured by visored helmets—a fleeting recognition kindled in the depth of shared desperation, a silent pact forged in the crucible of a dying starship crumbling into the void.

When at last they connected eye to eye across the gap of mere inches once spanning vast divides of culture, species and time... it felt less like two warriors poised on the brink of a battle won—as if instead they held the fragile, vulnerable heart of their strange new alliance captive between them. Each inhale became a communion, lungs filling with frigid night air until stars burned bright behind fluttering eyelids. Every exhalation whispered ancient truths across language barriers yet still managed to convey the raw depth of emotion pulsing between newfound allies brought together by fate's terrible whims.

Astrid's eyes remained locked on Mercer's own, pupils dilating like twin black holes swallowing stars against retinas shimmering with stardust. Entire ecosystems existed within these fiery storms...cosmologies born from entropy...

Abruptly, a sudden alert buzzed through the derelict bridge, mercifully sparing them from lapsing into philosophical meandering under the star's thrall. Warning lights flashed like a strobe across control panels reactivating spasmodically one-by-one.

"By the Throne," Astrid murmured, her mind struggling to fathom what could possibly radiate such intensity short of another stellar ignition.

As Mercer squinted, attempting to make sense of the searing phenomenon bearing down upon their crippled hulk, realization bloomed behind sun-dazzled vision like a shooting star blazing across the firmament—

The Starlight Marauder's distress beacon.

Forced offline upon first contact with the anomaly now visible, it had remained dormant until atmospheric decompression severed any hope of salvage...until Vex and Mercer stood poised at the precipice gazing upon total annihilation.

# Chapter 12: Gunfight on the Gantry

With Mercury's gravity already pulling at their heels, Leo and Astrid barely registered the jolt as the distressed Starlight Marauder's hull bucked beneath them, a reverberation more felt than heard in this vacuum. Yet even as aftershocks dissipated, they both immediately turned toward the ominous glare of impending doom now less than a parsec ahead of their vessel--too distant to discern details from this remove, but close enough for the eerie, pulsing brightness to scorch retinas and blind without UV filters.

It couldn't be natural. Neither Celestials nor quantum anomalies broadcast such power unfiltered. This was something else altogether, and if the Marauder's shields were compromised... One thing about pirates, their tech generally worked despite questionable priorities over safety standards. Without shields protecting them, that searing light alone would incinerate anything caught in its cone.

"What a fine mess we're in," Astrid quipped dryly, voice laced with the humor born of dire circumstances to stave off true panic. She swiftly scanned the main plotting display, her eyes widening at the rapid closure rate with the accreting celestial horror. "Looks like our ticket home just got jammed in high orbit beyond reach."

Leo nodded curtly, attention laser-focused on gauging escape vectors under gravity and propulsion constraints. No chance to sprint along the gantry outside in normal-Earth gee; they'd never keep up in this low-grav environment with acceleration dead opposite Mercury's pull. His hand involuntarily tightened around the grip of his silenced railcarbine as analysis ran through neural nets. One option presented itself amid the dire predictions: venting the Marauder's cargo holds to shift mass-center to reduce exposure during descent.

"You'd better prep our exit pods, Chief-- "

Astrid gestured emphatically before he could finish suggesting those escape vessels designed for one-shot hyperspace jumps, built with crash-and-abort protocols already engaged given the unfolding catastrophe. The corsair captain's urgency translated visually through clenched fists beating against thighs; frustration, fear, and acceptance wrestled for dominance across her battle-scarred visage.

"Escape pods aren't going anywhere, not with our engines offline either," she explained grimly. "Our only remaining option is EVA, suit up--"

Leo jerked a nod, intuition screaming for him to prioritize immediate action. He started toward the airlock, hand drifting back to tuck a spare energy cell into a pocket of his flight suit for emergency power. Astrid fell seamlessly into lockstep behind, her imposing presence making him acutely aware of every labored breath, every tiny tremor of expectation carrying the weight of imminent destruction. Even in silence, death loomed a mere second away.

The airlock hissed open, allowing them to clamber inside before the cycle started and the inner door sealed. On the other side awaited the cold dark of spacerock's surface, littered with chunks of asteroid and ice, waiting to skewer or crush them with equal indifference. Leo felt the hairs on his nape prickle yet steeled himself mentally for the punishing ordeal to come.

"...and pray there's solid ground close enough once we hit atmosphere," Astrid finished succinctly as the outer hatch cycled, the warning sirens dying along with the last dregs of life support back on their besieged vessel.

In reality, reaching terra firma on Mercury with standard 1G equipment wasn't feasible. Even discounted suits boasted grav-manipulation, far short of orbital-level inertia.

His ears rang from the alarm blasts and a metallic cacophony of screeching hull plating under assault. The Starlight Marauder seemed to scream around him, rebelling against its violent torments.

Leo's disoriented gaze tracked the streaking impact craters across astrogation holo-realities flickering to life within the cramped bridge, each one an unseen killing stroke delivered by unknown assailants cloaked in Mercury's shadowy depths. A fresh surge of crimson alarms pierced eardrums already stretched taut.

"We're taking too much damage for a routine boarding," Astrid intoned over comms, voice laced with clinical detachment belying the storm churning beneath. Her calloused fingers danced across console interfaces in a blur of diagnostics and fire control overrides. "Defensive measures are spent. Our only hope lies on the rock outside."

rdi snapped as the outer seal gave way with a violent shudder of the hull. Toxic starboard atmosphere boiled past, hurrying to escape with its telltale hiss before the cycle was cut short by catastrophic failure.

Behind him, Astrid followed like a black panther, fluid and deadly, her eyes locked firmly on escape as her thoughts no doubt teemed with escape strategies and contingency plans – after all, an ill-timed misstep outside might spell disaster just as surely as the hail of projectiles bearing down upon them now...

Into Mercury's Scorching Abyss

Astrid grabbed Leo's gloved hand, securing it tightly against hers even as she braced the other against the durasteel bulkhead to steady herself. They were pressed chest-to-chest in the cramped airlock, facing away from the hissing hatch seals and towards the yawning void. Each held their breath, hearts pounding in unison against the confines of their pressure suits.

Outside, stars blazed like diamonds scattered across velvet. The planet Mercury loomed larger with every passing second—a searing metal orb consumed by reflected solar fury. Astrid's gaze never wavered from their target, the tiny, fleeing dot representing their crippled ship rapidly dwindling beneath the horizon.

Leo checked their tether, giving a curt nod of confirmation before he switched his helmet comms to the external frequency. "Starlight Marauder, priority distress signal transmission—this is Commander Mercer and Captain Ross. We are about to attempt an emergency rendezvous at orbit twelve point niner." 

The pirate vessel's AI responded immediately, smooth contralto tones undeterred by the distance between ships: "Receiving, Commander. Initiate your approach vector now."

With a fierce twist of Astrid's wrist, they detached themselves from the station. Weightlessness enveloped them instantly, and for a brief moment, she allowed herself to savor the surreal beauty surrounding them before zeroing back in on their imperative mission. Astrid propelled herself and Leo through the void, each precise movement calculated to maintain precious momentum while conserving energy.

As Mercury loomed nearer, its blistering heat painted the inner surfaces of their helmets with sanguine hues and turned the dark expanse around them a hazy, hellish orange. Astrid knew time was running out—their brief window to connect with the Marauder was closing fast.

She initiated a final course correction, pushing off expertly to intercept their ship just shy of grazing Mercury's surface. Alarms began to screech warnings as Leo took the helm, working in tandem with Astrid despite the chasmic distances and centuries separating their origins.

Their ships collided with a jarring metallic crash that sent bone-jarring seismic shockwaves pulsating through the hull—dampened but still violent thanks to the superior engineering of the marauder class. Smoke wafted, and sparks erupted from compromised power conduits, yet both vessels remained structurally intact.

"Well played, Captain," Leo radioed over the ship-to-ship channel, grinning wearily as Astrid helped wrest him through the gaping breach.

"We're not out of this yet, Commander," Astrid shot back, already assessing the damage and plotting their next steps. Her voice carried an edge, both exhaustion-fueled and battle-hardened—a testament to the unforgiving nature of their odyssey so far. "There's still debris and possible hostile craft in the area..."

Leo merely nodded sagely, his visor tinting crimson as he inspected the ruinous interior of what once was their cockpit. The charnel house of twisted steel framing, shattered consoles, and scorched upholstery spoke volumes about the hellfires that had ravaged their stolen Kestrel transport before its desperate plunge back into deep space to meet Astrid's rescue gamble head-on.

"I know," he rasped before trailing off, struggling visibly to keep the despair behind his masks. Even now, with death's dark shadow finally held at bay due to Astrid and the Starlight's intervention, grief could come later—and would likely hit harder when the adrenaline receded.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo cradled his ruined right forearm, a grimace tugging at his lips. Though not actively bleeding, the charred skin cracked open whenever he tried to flex, stoking waves of pain against his will. He squinted toward the ruptured viewport, where starlight struggled to infiltrate the clouded plenum of gas and ionized dust that surrounded them—a thin, ethereal blanket of interstellar haze drifting on solar wind across billions of miles of empty cosmos.

"Well, Captain Vex..." His voice croaked like sandpaper on bone. "...looks like we're stuck. No navigational data left to steer by...no fuel to make a break for it either. And it'll take weeks if not months just to scrounge up replacement parts—if you can find a black market deal maker with access to Type-2A shields and maneuvering thrusters." 

The ship creaked around them, settling into her final rest like a bird losing flight feathers, unable to take wing ever again. Astrid nodded soberly, eyes narrowed into glints of appraisal within her silver mask—as though sizing up any potential weaknesses she might exploit in her own predicament, trapped alongside the alien warlord who had brought this on herself. For good reason, Leo knew—that same ruthlessness had earned her title as a corsair legend, making deals with demons and ghosts where most sane beings would draw red lines.

"The local stars don't show much promise for repairs anyway," Astrid allowed after a long pause, voice echoing quietly from her suit comm system. "No significant gravity wells, and definitely no jump gates out here this side of the Orion Spur." Her gloved hand found his injured forearm, giving it a reassuring squeeze despite her own evident weariness etched into every angle and line of her posture. A surprising gesture, given their tumultuous history—but then again it was only fitting of a woman who defied borders and allegiances where loyalty was a currency paid in blood. Still, he felt a fleeting spark of gratitude in spite of himself.

"What does one do after a crash, then?" Leo muttered bleakly, blinking away vision distortions. At his query, the viewport suddenly flared bright enough to eclipse his pupils momentarily, bathing the gantry in stark relief as they shielded their eyes against the searing light.

"No idea," Astrid admitted as the flare faded slowly, casting everything in a diffuse luminosity that seemed almost surreal amidst the wreckage. In this sterile realm without echoes where vacuum's chill darkness clung to each surface with unyielding persistence—soundless, unscented, utterly alien—the pair stood frozen, staring at the glowing portal now visible beyond the jagged opening previously concealed by hull plating.

An unmistakable wormhole signature—it pulsed rhythmically as though alive, swirling with aurora-shimmering quantum foam in impossible hues that danced across spectrums normally seen by human eyes. Without bothering to consult charts or manuals, an inexplicable sense told Leo they were witnessing some arcane phenomenon well outside the purview of even their star-mapped universe—and yet...

"...according to all known models, this configuration suggests a stable gateway connecting two regions possessing vastly different energies in space-time." Astrid murmured softly once her gaze adjusted to focus past the mesmerizing display, tone tinged with a mix of amazement and foreboding. Whatever lurked on the other end of this tunnel piercing dimensions unseen—be it paradise, apocalypse, or something far more sinister beneath classification—Leo understood implicitly that no decision taken here would remain purely their own.

# Chapter 13: Breaching the High Security Block

Commander Leo Mercer strained against the massive shock-mounted servos securing the gantry to his rig, watching as Astrid writhed atop a tangled mass of severed power conduits. Flames licked at the frayed edge of his flight suit, heat radiating through the carbon-fiber mesh to scorch his thighs.

"Hold steady!" she panted between gritted teeth, reaching for the blow torch strapped to his thigh.

Leo couldn't spare breath for reply. His core muscles screamed with sustained effort as he tried to keep the servos locked fast. The wormhole's light pulse thrummed a staccato beat in harmony with his pounding heart, filling his vision with an otherworldly glow. Sweat poured down his face, but evaporated instantly in the sub-zero climate before he could feel its warmth.

"Astrid—" he choked out warningly, noticing her gaze had drifted back towards the pulsating vortex swallowing half the viewport. In a sudden burst of insight, Leo realized her eyes glowed with a feverish brightness, reflections of the celestial anomalies dancing within.

In a fluid motion, he activated the built-in hydraulic overrides, allowing the servos to retract while maintaining control. As the restraints eased, Leo lunged forward, grabbing Astrid's wrist to halt her aim at the portal. Her blowtorch hissed out a futile plume of sparks into a void devoid of oxygen.

"Don't risk firing that near the wormhole," Leo gritted. "We don't know how it'll interact with our tech or radiation shielding!"

Astrid jerked her arm free, but he caught hold of her other hand in a vice-like grip. She met his gaze with fiery defiance, lips curled in a snarl. A current of raw electricity crackled through their joined bodies under the starscraper's artificial ambient field—a potent mixture of attraction and resentment.

"You always do this, Leo," Astrid snapped. "Micro-manage until you stifle every creative thought or daring impulse I have! Just because your primitive linear mentality can't grasp the implications"

"You think I'm restraining innovation?" Leo shot back fiercely. "I'm trying not to get us killed off in a catastrophic experiment we're woefully unprepared for! When it comes to your instincts and hunches, I trust them. But this is beyond either of our paygrades. We need information and strategy before—"

The wormhole flickered violently, casting an eerie strobe effect over the duo and their ravaged surroundings. It made Astrid's enhanced irises seem to swallow whole clusters of the chromatic fire raging inside the singularity. For a moment, Leo swore his vision blurred as if distorted by some unfathomable curvature of space. Astrid's features warped too, reflected in the plasma dance as if they both existed outside the three-dimensional bounds of reality in those chaotic instants.

They stared at each other transfixed, neither fully present in the momentary confluence of temporal planes and energy flux. Then, in the next cycle of the wormhole's rhythmic spasms, Leo shook his head to regain focus. Their gazes finally broke apart as if electrified from a charged arc.

"...we breach the adjacent compartment," Astro finished lowly, pulling herself up with trembling arms onto the crumbled husk of the airlock door. It creaked alarmingly as she put weight upon it. The metallic groans echoed strangely in the emptiness of space, magnified by the acoustic dampeners long since destroyed. "Find whatever hardware and data you can salvage to improve our chances of manipulating this thing safely.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo watched, heart thrumming, as Astrid climbed atop the disintegrating airlock hatch. Her stance was precarious, knees bent beneath her, one hand anchoring while the other grasped for purchase anywhere in the mangled metal. The wormhole continued its frenzied pulsing beyond, casting shifting hues across their haggard bodies like some cosmic, maddening disco light show. The silence outside the Marauder was absolute, void of even the comforting hiss of life support - the abyssal vacuum embracing them without respite.

"How...sturdy do ya think that'll hold?" Leo ventured, voice barely above a whisper against the sonic wasteland stretching out from the ship. His eyes remained fixed on Astrid's lithe form perched precariously above the fraying threshold. Even through her skintight spacesuit, he could sense her physical strain, the labored breathing and tensing muscles as she sought to stabilize herself. He understood that desperation-fueled resilience all too well.

Astrid flashed him a grim smile over her shoulder, not breaking eye contact. "Guess I should've brought my trusty ladder, eh? Just gotta hope enough of this junk holds together." She paused, considering the implications. "Considering we got dropped into here unprepped and still recovering from the fall... might be our best bet so far."

"Falls ain't exactly my strong suit," Leo muttered ruefully, running a nervous hand through his wind-tousled hair. But there was no time for self-pity. Any second the entire structure around Astrid could plummet like a dying warbird into the hungry jaws of the singularity below. Against such unimaginable forces, a few more tons of scrap steel didn't mean much.

"Astro—"
"What?" Her gaze snapped back to meet his, amber orbs alight with a primal mix of grit and fear.

"This feels...bad. Like tempting fate or something." He held her stare, willing her to understand the old-fashioned gut check happening amidst the stars. "We're already skating damn close to certain doom out here. Letting you balance on top of a broken airlock feels like inviting a little extra catastrophe..."

His words trailed off as realization struck him like a plasma pulse to the chest. What was he even saying? That they should just give up, retreat back to the relative safety of their crippled vessel and pray fate went easy on them? No, hell no. He couldn't let those cowardly thoughts take root. Not when Astrid was out there risking everything because one crazy risk mattered more than staying alive. A feeling akin to shame gnawed at his resolve.

"It's okay, Commander. I know what I'm doing here," Astrid said firmly, as if sensing his growing inner turmoil. Those honeyed words carried the subtle cadence of command rather than camaraderie this time. Beneath her tone lay an undercurrent of 'back the hell off,' letting Leo know he'd tread a fine line as her second-in-command aboard the Marauder.

The heavy silence that followed was oppressive, straining with the weight of expectations and raw, unspoken emotions bubbling just beneath the surface. The wormhole's erratic flashes seemed to pulse in sync with the racing beats of their hearts. Finally, unable to bear any longer the seething storm of frustration, resentment, and admiration battling within, Leo pushed himself upright, hands bracing against his thighs.

"Good. Because we've got a job to finish and an Empire to bring to its goddamn knees," he managed through clenched teeth, the old military cadence breaking free despite his better judgment. "Let's get moving.

✦ ✦ ✦

The clanging clangor of rapid hatches announced their entry into the heavily fortified sector of Kyros Orbital's research hub. Lieutenant Saez, eyes wide with a mix of apprehension and excitement, fumbled with his plasma rifle, trying not to get trampled in the chaotic advance of the Marauder's boarding party.

"We're in deep now," Leo muttered, voice barely audible over the rattling of armor plates and shouting commands. His gut twisted like a corkscrew, but he steeled himself to face whatever terrors awaited beyond the airlock. The flickering blue lights cast eerie shadows along the corridor's sealed metal bulkheads, as if some malevolent entity lurked in the darkness, waiting to claim souls for the ages.

Behind him, Astrid's boots clicked sharply against the decking, each deliberate step exuding confidence born from years of defying death. Her scent, a heady blend of cool sweat, sharp ozone, and an unseen essence uniquely hers, tantalized Leo's senses, a fleeting reminder of the perilous game they played so intimately entangled.

Time stretched, distorting the rhythm of pulse and breath. Each labored inhale was bitter, metallic – recycled air thickened by fear, adrenaline, and the acrid tang of ion-scraped metal. Every exhale shook the mask covering Leo's face, a frail barrier against the choking void outside. The silence was oppressive, punctuated only by muffled alarms issuing from distant nodes and the heavy rasp of their breathing.

Leo's hands trembled slightly, betraying the turmoil threatening to unravel his composure. Memories crashed anew – his first spacewalk, the horrific loss of the Challenger, Gagarin's triumphant orbit... all jumbled into a sense-deadening cacophony. It was almost too late when Astrid grabbed his arm, hauling him forward.

"Hold up, Lieutenant!" she snapped, her voice crisp and commanding amidst the chaos. They'd reached an armored bulkhead marked with imperial crests and warning placards. A pulsing energy field seared across the surface, humming with the promise of instantaneous disintegration for any daredevil foolish enough to breach the defenses uninvited.

Astrid's fingers danced deftly across a small holographic control panel mounted nearest Leo's shoulder. Vectors converged, calculations sped along hidden data streams, and an oscillating resonance began to build within the shielding emitters. The energy mesh danced wildly, sputtering weakly as Astrid bypassed the security protocols.

She glanced back over her shoulder, eyes blazing with triumph and something else, darker still beneath, that made Leo's heart thud erratically against his ribcage. "Ready?" Without giving him a chance to respond, she triggered the overload resonance, sending an avalanche of turbulent energy crashing through the shield wall.

In a burst of strobing light, crackling atmosphere, and the smell of scorched micro-circuits, they squeezed through the breach. On the other side, they found themselves in a narrow corridor lined with closed blast doors, pulsing life support conduits, and towering storage pods loaded with top-secret project crates.

"Well, damn," Leo breathed, still squinting against the afterglow of their incursion, when a sudden, piercing scream shattered the momentary hush. It echoed down the passageway, a chilling howl that turned Leo's blood to ice. Whatever had made that unearthly noise was close, fast approaching – and far from friendly.

Astrid's gaze locked onto Leo's with an implicit understanding. Their mission had just acquired a whole lot Deadlier.

✦ ✦ ✦

CHAPTER 13: BREACHING THE HIGH SECURITY BLOCK

The concussive force of their transit through the shield door hurled Leo forward, slamming him against the wall. Pain ignited across his knuckles where he'd instinctively braced his impact suit. He slid down, catching himself on his heels, and stared wide-eyed at the chaotic corridor beyond the smoking breach. Emergency lighting flickered fitfully, casting long shadows across the narrow passageway.

Leo's breath sounded harsh in his ears amid the echoing thrum of damaged shielding and suppressed alarm klaxons. Glancing over, he saw Astrid step out of the glow, already scanning their surroundings with cold predatory interest. Her black hair rippled like nightfall beneath the pale light. Her expression - lean-lippered focus - spoke of steel-sharpened reflexes and intellect honed by decades of predation in the stars.

"Well, damn," he murmured, struggling to regain his bearings amidst the disorienting kaleidoscope of alien technology. Their daring penetration of the secret block already felt like walking the razor's edge of danger.

Stroking back sweat-slick hair, Leo pointed toward the open storage pods lining the corridor. Each crate was clearly labeled Project: Orion-Skyguard. Classified intel and advanced weapons perhaps? He wondered what nefarious plans the Emissaries might be constructing behind these sealed doors.

Just then, Astrid's head whipped around sharply, features contorting in a grimace of alarm. Following her gaze, Leo caught sight of movement further down the passage - faint outlines darting between towering tech cylinders.

"What in–?"

A gut-wrenching scream tore the air, the cry of something primal and tormented. It sent icy pricks racing up Leo's spine as the echoes reverberated off the metal deck. That awful noise wasn't machinery malfunctioning - it was definitely alive...

And headed straight for them.

Astrid's lips flattened to a ruthless line. Her rifle snapped free from its holder as she edged to the corridor's center, pressing into the shadowy bulk of a supply pod. The howls grew louder, closer, until Leo could discern frantic, bestial panting punctuated by snarls born from unutterable pain and fury.

He fumbled for his own pulse carbine, finger hovering reluctantly above the trigger. Whatever beast this was, they were defenseless in the cramped, exposed corridor without cover. He prayed it was just some deranged research subject; but the unnatural shrieks kindled a sickening suspicion that the creatures hiding among the high-security assets might have designs more malignant than mere experimentation gone sour...

Astral's fiery amber gaze met Leo's terrified blue stare. Though not a word passed between them, the message transmitted in those searing seconds was unmistakable - we're in for the fight of our lives. The floor trembled under claw-beats, warning them barely a second before a massive, lopsided creature burst into view around the next bend, preceded by a halo of reflected emergency lights...

# Chapter 14: No Time for Tears

Leo froze as the monstrous shape erupted into view, a nightmarish apparition caged in a halo of flickering light reflections. Bulging, malnourished haunches propelled the grotesque amalgamation forward on an elongated, misshapen gait that seemed to defy logic. Its scabrous mass of gray skin stretched over bulging, asymmetrical limbs, knotted tendon and sinew visible beneath the mottled epidermis like a dissected anatomy chart come to life. Pulsing crimson orbs dominated the creature's skull, fixating on its new quarry with a primal fervor devoid of intelligence. Twin horns protruded at precarious angles from the macabre cranium, hooked like daggers intended to disembowel and tear.

The beast's hoarse, agonized panting reverberated along the metal passageway—a chilling symphony announcing its arrival. Leo felt a rivulet of cold sweat trickle down his spine despite the frigid chill of the abandoned station. This wasn't some lab rat or genetically engineered critter run amok. Whatever unnatural abomination pursued them had evolved or been birthed under the harsh, adverse conditions prevalent here.

"Holy shit," Leo breathed involuntarily, fighting a sudden wave of queasiness as the creature's fetid stench wafted down the corridor, reeking of rotten meat, ammonia, and charred bone.

Astrid exhaled slowly through gritted teeth as if reining in a temperamental animal. She tightened her grip on the pulse carbine, aiming past the monstrosity toward the dark recesses where more like it could lurk. "We need shelter and fast. If they've got numbers..."

She didn't need to finish the thought. They both knew their meager weapons and minimal shielding wouldn't stand a chance against a large pack of such formidable, vicious specimens. The creatures would overwhelm them quickly should they be cornered.

Leo nodded curtly, adrenaline spiking as he flicked his carbine's power setting to concentrated disruptor pulses rather than scattering rounds to deter but not harm potential survivors. He'd take any opportunity to disable these beasts, limiting the threat to themselves.

"Ahead on the portside—there's a maintenance room we can barricade." Astrid pointed with her gun barrel. "Stay close and watch my six."

Without waiting for a response, the pirate captain charged forward, leading them on a perilous dash past their one-time terror through the labyrinthine passages leading to the storage compartment. Leo followed doggedly, keeping the creature's bulk near their rear as a buffer against further attacks. His heart hammered against his rib cage, pulse throbbing in his ears as they pressed onward through the dank, echoing confines of the derelict moonbase. Even in the gloom of the corridors, the acrid stench clung to him like a noxious wet blanket—making it difficult to focus on anything other than his racing breath and the metallic taste of dread saturating his mouth. Every instinct cried out for them to run faster, but Leo reined in the impulse, forcing himself to maintain pace alongside Astrid. Rushing blind could lead to a dead end, traps, or ambushes he couldn't defend against effectively.

As they skidded into the maintenance room, Leo slammed and locked the reinforced hatch behind them. Astrid wasted no time surveying the dimly lit chamber—its sterile linoleum floors gleaming with an otherworldly sheen in the scattered emergency lighting. Metal workbenches lined the periphery, littered with rusting diagnostic tools and discarded components of long-abandoned equipment.

✦ ✦ ✦

"I've got enough scrap for repairs—this'll do as shelter for a few hours," Astrid declared, already stripping the useless machinery to salvage parts. Sweat beaded her brow, glistening in the emergency lights casting long, eerie shadows across the metal floor. Kneeling to rummage through a pile of discarded circuit boards, she glanced up at Leo sidelong, a hint of accusation in her gaze.

"What now, hero?" The amusement in her voice had a sharper edge of sarcasm hanging above it like barbed wire. "Got any bright ideas saving the day?"

Leo bristled at her tone—it was the first crack in her normally tightlipped composure since they'd escaped. Stepping closer, he fought to keep his anger simmering beneath the surface rather than erupting. "My aim isn't to rescue a damsel-in-distress, Captain Ross... nor is winning your admiration my primary motivation." He crouched down beside her, scrutinizing the array of components strewn about the floor. 

"The question is simply where we can expect pursuit next. Tracking this facility has likely taken more resources than our quarry anticipated—which means they might reassess priorities now that they've got your ship in custody. Could be seeking some leverage play to regain her mobility before giving chase again..."

Astrid snorted, waving a hand dismissively as a flickering glance crossed her face. "Speculating won't bring Zara to heel. She's made her intentions clear—a pawn in whatever dirty game between the guilds—until one of you plays by their rules. Or she drops us in the nearest dustbin." Her lips twisted bitterly.

"Well, Z didn't grow the Starlight's reputation with patience." The captain rose fluidly, muscles coiling underneath her fitted leather wear as she began selecting component parts from their haphazard piles. "We either find a way to retake control outright or slip free under their noses while they're cocky, thinkin' I'm outgunned and helpless without her."

"I get what drives you, Vex—rekindling the ghost of your old rebellion; having the upper hand again—but that ain't strategy when you're outnumbered." Leo stood too, folding his arms over his chest as he faced her steadily. He refused to engage with her aggression head-on. No matter how many daggers flashed in her eyes, he could show none in return. "Clever pirates evolve, adapt—your approach worked when the odds were better aligned, but throwing dice in a high-stakes casino isn't leadership. It's recklessness bordering on suicidal."

The hiss of Astrid's exhale sounded suspiciously like a startled gasp—the fire in her gaze briefly banks, replaced by stunned incomprehension before flickering back to full flame. "So now you're counseling me on command?" Venom dripped heavily off each word. "Funny—I could've used guidance from someone with half your arrogance when the ODF was ripping my crew apart...but you know what they say: pride comes before defeat."

"That's not what I meant!" Leo raised his hands in exasperation, searching for the right words amidst the escalating standoff. But every attempt felt like pouring gasoline on this burning powder keg. "I understand the rage fueling your vengeance; I'm just trying to inject some semblance of a plan here! We both want the same thing: freedom and reclaiming our vessels, though we differ—"

"Differ?" Astrid's laugh cut across him, raw and humorless. "Hell, that's one way to put it.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leo's protest died as it hit the wall of Astrid's glare, frozen mid-air between them like a challenging gauntlet. Her fists clenched at her sides, knuckles dragging white against the black synth-leather of her flightsuit. Tendrils of heat haze eddied around her in the cramped confines of the cockpit. Sweat beaded at her temples and trickled down her jawline in rivulets, shining like tears she refused to shed.

The Starlight Marauder bucked beneath their feet as another barrage shook the hull plates, threatening to throw them off balance entirely. Metal groaned and acrid smoke bit at their lungs, carried in on the turbulent air current from the breached compartments.

Astrid's boots scrabbled for purchase on the wet decking as another volley lit up the viewport behind her, searing blue-white streaks etching across the inky void. She wrenched her gaze free of Leo's, squinting through the sting of salt in her eyes to fix on the looming form of Arcturus II ahead.

"We're going to get through this," she forced out, voice wavering between determination and ragged self-doubt. "I didn't come so far just to—"

Her words broke off in a choked snarl as the bridge display erupted into warnings, klaxons blaring in urgent protest. Alarms flooded every console—a devastating concatenation of engine overload, failing thrusters, crippled life support, and crippling radiation leaks, all converging to paint a stark picture of impending doom.

Astrid lunged forward, grabbing frantic handfuls of hair in desperation as panic clawed its way up her throat. She yanked out a comm-link, shouting over the cacophony. "Ross to engineer! Get us stabil—"

Silence fell as suddenly as the chaos had burst forth, leaving only heavy breathing and the ominous creak of strained metal in its wake. Astrid collapsed back into her chair, shoulders slumped in defeat—except those arms still gripped tight onto her skull, nails scraping against scalp, face twisted in anguish beyond words. The realization dawned in agonizing slow motion, horror twisting her features.

Their window had slammed shut. Arcturus II already filled the viewport like an oppressive demon made flesh, looming dark and malevolent against the glittering stars. There would be no reprieve, no chance to make amends, reforge alliances, or outrun the storm. Only the cold embrace of oblivion waiting to consume them all.

Astrid rocked back and forth, small broken sounds escaping her lips like lost sobs in the vacuum. And then came Leo's bootfalls thudding deliberately along the catwalk to halt before her. He bent at the waist to scoop her up from her meltdown, cradling Astrid against his chest like she was precious cargo, not the fearsome battle-hardened commander who'd commandeered his ship less than a stellar cycle ago.

"What kind of fool does this to themselves?" he ground out, incredulity shading into something deeper, almost gentle, as he held her trembling form against his solid heat. His scent enveloped her—fresh rain, old leather, and that spark of electric danger she couldn't seem to quit. For once, Astrid met his gaze without challenge or deflection, surrender written in the vulnerability pooling in her mismatched eyes.

"No mercy," she whispered, the admission ripped from her like confessional bleeding. "Maybe death's mercy will be sweeter. Let's just...

✦ ✦ ✦

The weight of their world hung heavy in each other's arms as they stood there, isolated by fate yet more intimately connected than any ally or lover could ever be. Above them, the vast panorama of nebulas and distant civilizations wheeled on unseen axes, a celestial indifferent to their insignificance. Silent as a tomb, their spaceships drifted ghostly amidst the starry expanse like spectral reminders of everything they were swiftly losing.

It was ironic that within mere lightminutes they possessed technology to breach the fabric of space and time itself. Quantum warps were humanity's greatest invention and darkest horror - an alchemical marriage of gravity and exotic energy. It granted near instantaneously access to every corner of the Cosmos but it did so at a terrible cost. Any vessel utilizing such power left a scar upon its reality – a wormhole that unraveled and regurgitated fragments of unprocessed spacetime. The further the quantum leap, the more unstable those rips became till finally, inevitably, they imploded, snuffing the ship and crew into oblivion along with countless parsecs of extraneous matter and information.

That cosmic trapdoor had yawned open right beneath Luna Nine and dragged them screaming down its light years-long throat. As if fate's cruel fist was twisting the knife, their very survival depended on outrunning those annihilating rifts before they closed forever behind them. Problem was nobody knew where those destructive whirlpools appeared or could predict with certainty when...or where...the final black hole of destruction would materialize to devour the fleeing remnants of their civilization.

Leo clutched Astrid tighter as the awful truth echoed through him, every bone chilled, insides lurching like a riptide pulling a swimmer down into frigid depths. If Luna Nine succumbed before reaching the nearest safe haven...they'd be reduced to subatomic particles that even light wouldn't carry far. Their individual consciousnesses scattered across the universe like flecks of stardust would vanish into irrelevance while still conscious long enough to comprehend forever-witness the void swallowing home worlds whole.

"What are we going to do, Vex?" his raw voice crackled through helmet comms but the question wasn't really meant for her. It was an appeal to a higher authority, a plea to stars now nothing more than distant pinpricks against eternity's bleak canvas.

In response, a frantic sensor alert flared red across the helm displays - unexpected astrogational data flickering onto several scopes simultaneously like frantic static whispers through subspace radio antennae. Leo squinted at the screens, trying to decipher the anomaly until he snapped head-whirling about to face Astrid whose expression mirrored his own shock and trepidation:

"...is that..." he gulped, struggling to speak clearly past the dryness blooming fast in his throat "...an artificial gravity well? In system...but impossible...those signatures don't match any known technology..."

Astrid set to work checking and cross-checking with urgency mounting in each movement while behind them the dying sun bleached whatever remaining light remained on the hull from the Starlight Marauder to ghostly blue.

"It can't be," the commander muttered, shaking her head. "Something's feeding those readings false data. That's how wormholes appear – pseudogravitational lenses masking the true extent and instability."

She spun to face back towards the viewscreen which now displayed a sickening distortion – space itself seemingly churning and belching chaos as if vomiting back something...somebeing from the deepest recesses of void.

# Chapter 15: The Launch Bay Ejection

Shudders rippled through the Starlight Marauder's deckplating as it jolted free from the dying colony ship, inertial dampeners already straining against the sudden disparity in mass ratios. Gravity generators hummed ominously, compensatory fields warping into existence around the fleeing pirate frigate to counteract the loss of Centaur's ponderous pull. 

Leo felt the violent lurch first through seat restraints digging painful lines into his torso, helmet clamped down tightly over eyes squeezing shut lest stray photons pierce retinas. Then the cacophony of battle outside the hangar doors erupted, an impromptu symphony of laser fire screeching along the spectrum, explosive fragmentation pummeling in earsplitting drumroll, metallic shrieks protesting overstressed structural integrity. The Marauder's shields hissed like smoldering brakes fighting to ablate incoming ordinance and protect vulnerable internals.

"All hands, strap in!" Astrid's gravelly command clawed its way through Leo's helmet, echoing in auditory implants linked to comms circuitry. Though not fully cognizant yet, even slumbering nerves and reflex-hardened muscles reacted instinctively to crisis, limbs knotting together in tight ball as if trying to contain the primal fear gnawing at gut. Not fear specifically of death per se – they both had lived through far worse – but dread born from a nameless existential horror lurking just beyond perception.

Outside, the abyss rushed in, eager to reclaim the vanishing metal husk of humanity's failed last stand. Inky vastness stretched to infinity in every direction, devoid of stars save the solitary maroon hulk of Centaur eclipsing what little sunken light struggled through atmosphere. The absence of background noise was equally unsettling – no soft hiss of breathing or gentle hum of engines but only the acrid tang of burnt metals and ozone dancing on the chill of liquid helium thrusters exhaling their chemical waste into the frozen emptiness.

Inch by inch, yard by agonizing yard, the freighter shrank in the viewscreen, its fading angular silhouette receding towards pointlessness. A momentary respite came amidst the mayhem, giving the battered marauder crew short-lived reprieve to glance up, catch their breaths even as ragged gasps wheezed in oxygen masks. But reprieve soon turned bittersweet when stark reality revealed themselves reflected back in polished armor plating strewn across viewport.

Flanking the Marauder like menacing piranhas darting up the flank of a wounded whale were six gleaming cruisers of unknown origin with sleek, obsidian hulls bristling razor-sharp spines and arrays of pulsing weapons modules. Even the limited resolution granted by passive sensors could detect no human presence on these vessels – whatever occupied them, it moved with alien fluidity and purposeful intent, as chilling as any nightmare. 

"We cannot outrun," Astrid breathed, speaking so low that Leo almost thought the words were his own private paranoia. Fumbling fingers danced nimbly over the navigation console, seeking optimal trajectory through clouds of debris strewn across the horizon like confetti after a bloodied riot while fighters continued to probe like sharks hunting survivors from doomed escape pods.

"S-soon as we clear—" another jagged roar rocked the starboard flank and Leo heard panicked cry cut off in splintered screams over local comms feed as a plasma bolt pierced engine housing spraying molten shrapnel through compartment —

Leonidas 'Leo' Mercer shook off fragmented images of burning flesh with effort similar to forcing open rusted safe deposit box, focusing once more on maintaining situational awareness though the clammy grip of adrenaline

Chapter 15: The Launch Bay Ejection

"Damn you, damn me, damn this hellhole!" Commander Mercer snarled, voice cracking between gritted teeth as he clung desperately to the wreckage-strewn exterior of the hijacked liner. Explosions blossomed across his panoramic view in retina-searing lurches of scarlet and incandescent violet, each brighter than Mars at zenith. The deafening cacophony assaulting his senses—shattering impacts, blistering heat pulses, shrieks of tortured metal—struggled for relevance amidst the eerie stillness of the vacuum. Not a whisper of wind, not the faintest crackle of electricity, only the brutal force of projectiles hammering the cerulean darkness.

Mercer twisted half-turned along the struts supporting the ruptured boarding airlock, searching frantically for an optical signal from their captors. Astrid had warned him of the pirates' ruthless tactics—their penchant for abandoning even valuable prisoners adrift as space junk—but he couldn't shake the compulsion rising within him. Unspoken code of command, ingrained since childhood in starry-eyed cadet fantasies. Duty required him to know what hit them before making plans to dodge or destroy...

A sudden tug yanked his arms up beside his head, hurling him into a wild spin down a pockmarked tunnel of torn metal girders toward the distant terminus where escaping gas vented in shimmering pearls into the abyss. The g-forces pinned him rigid against the strut, breath ragged and ears popping as pressure dropped precipitously outward—hurtling him toward oblivion at several thousand meters per second. His bodyweight shifted as the ship's gravity died away, flinging him forward now...now...

Suddenly a massive hand clamped on the back of his flight suit just above the collar bones, halting his tumble mid-air. A momentary daze washed over him at the shocking contact, eyes bulging involuntarily behind transparent shield goggles...then understanding kicked in. He'd nearly forgotten—his captain, his partner, his rescuer—had done similarly impossible acrobatics aboard the liner itself earlier, leaping vast distances and defying physics with every desperate stride through burning corridors as they fled their enemies. What once seemed superhuman now felt all too grounded: this woman was capable of anything—had proved it already under dures he could hardly comprehend.

"What?" Astrid demanded between clenched teeth via the neural implant link embedded beneath his tongue. "Can it, Cowboy! I ain't got time nor patience left to play hero damsel today."

He forced reluctant laughter past his dry throat, managing a gruff chuckle even as bone-jarring turbulence buffeted them mercilessly between grasping claws of fractured hull plates. "Thought maybe I was too much meat for ya pirates to enjoy at leisure on your kill tally board," he retorted sarcastically even as an explosive fireball lit her faceplate almost supernaturally bright. For one breathless instant Mercer swore he saw the glint of tears lurking in those storm-gray eyes behind the tinted polymer.

"Bullshit," she spat. Just that. Two vicious syllables, but they packed more vehemence to sting into his eardrum than any rebuke ever hurled from superior officer or ex-lover. There it was plain and simple—a reminder of who owned his loyalty, at least in this precarious hell-hole beyond the reaches of Empire law—and she was right, goddamn it, they didn't have time. Even as they tumbled further outwards from the crippled liner, its dwindling silhouette resolving into a dying ember among scattered asteroids, another trio of angular

✦ ✦ ✦

Mercer's blood ran cold as a sudden jolt shook the airframe. Pressure gauges flared crimson across the dashboard's augmented display, warning them their failing suit seals wouldn't hold long against the freezing void. Astrid's voice snapped like a whip through the comms, tone sharp as razors:

"Hulls breached starboard side! Multiple structural collapses in progress—"
A deafening whine drowned out the rest as the Marauder's repulsor core surged to maximum thrust in an emergency ascent maneuver. Searing heat blistered Mercer's cheekbones—the acceleration pressing him hard back into the console, stars blurring into blue-white streaks outside. But there was no respite; they must've hit some unknown debris field en route, judging by the violent lurches and groans wrenching their battered ship from side to side.

A burst of searing ozone stung his nostrils. Alarms chirped frantic warnings amidst crackles and groans echoing through the lifelines and struts. Mercer's heart threatened to seize up in his chest as the numbers scrolled relentlessly downward on two key systems—

Main Fuel Reserve: 
78% → 62% → 46%

Starboard Gyro Stabilizers:

Operational → Reducing Power → Failure Imminent

Grim recognition sank in—theirs might well be a suicide run, catapulting a fuel-starved spacecraft without functional stabilizers straight into open space. Unless...

The idea seized him like a vision from the pits of madness—or maybe salvation offered by the chaos itself. Mercer jerked his gaze to Vex, mind racing; he needed convincing, needed her onside. And quick—because if not soon... 

The Marauder bucked savagely under them once more then again, throwing the two of them off balance before slamming them face-first against restraints. Astrid roared something incoherent over the howl of tortured metal, silver hair whipping past Mercer's strained eyes. She kicked free of the harness with savage force, ripping herself toward the cockpit doorway just ahead in a flurry of leather, cloth, and flex-weave armor.

With a snarl of frustration mixed with grim determination, Mercer fumbled after hers, heedless of his ripped uniform flapping wildly about his legs and forearms now unmoored within the centrifugal forces. Pain from strained ligaments in his shoulders only sharpened focus—and desperation. A few vital seconds lost meant an early grave trapped behind dead inertial dampeners. It was down to raw muscle and sheer nerve next.

Outside the cockpit, stars swirled in sickening spirals, their constellations bleeding towards infinity within distorted arcs of shattered atmosphere. Mercer had to think, had to plan despite the screaming need in his gut urging immediate action. But what choice did they have besides a catastrophic exit? No escape this way... unless—

His gaze snapped around to lock onto a nearby hulk barely perceptible in the darkness beside them—the burnt skeleton of some other craft, likely vaporized in the chaotic crossfire. Then everything clicked into place.

Grabbing onto a severed strut jutting out from the wreckage, Mercer struggled to haul himself closer to the mangled hull, feet scrabbling clumsily against the outer skin covered in slick hydraulic coolant residue. This was insane—it felt mad. Astrid watched his antics warily, lips peeled back in a furious grimace etched upon pale cheeks, fingers curled tight around her pulse rifle.

"The damned thing could implode on us and spray us to atoms even if we manage to rip free...

✦ ✦ ✦

With agonizing effort, Mercer managed to pull himself hand over scraping elbow along the disintegrating hull, using every fiber to resist Earth's brutal gravitational tug. Coolant dripped like icy tears across his face as he wrenched himself over a jagged metal ridge to clamber atop an exposed section of fuselage frame.

Stellar pinpricks still whirred like pirouetting dervishes against inky blackness beyond broken viewport seals. But for a fleeting moment, his vantage revealed something far more shocking than the war-torn void outside—a pinpoint of radiant light hanging steady just off their starboard bow. Mercer squinted against the glare until his brain reluctantly processed it. That wasn't any known comet or shooting star: it was a ship, or at least its engine flare cutting cleanly through emptiness like a laser scalpel.

"Astro—look!" He jabbed a triumphant finger before he second-guessed the urgency of their situation. "Maybe if we—"

"Oh, holy fuck," Astrid breathed, spotting the incoming vessel alongside him and instantly grasping its implications. Her features twisted into a mix of disbelief and dread. Even through her exosuit, she felt an involuntary shiver crawl like frost up her spinal column.

They were less than 200 kilometers away, well within missile range even without thrusting flares painting the darkness. A larger ship by at least three-fold compared to theirs, it resolved into sleek lines and angular armor plating as it surged relentlessly forward. Not military hardware by the looks—the streamlined design betrayed corsairs or privateers instead, built for speed rather than heavy fire. But Mercer knew better than to underestimate raiders who could afford such premium technology.

"It's a heavy-hitter alright..." he muttered, scouring its deadly profile inch by deadly inch. "Looks like they're heading straight for us, intent on investigating whatever drew their notice."

Astrid bit her lower lip hard enough to taste blood, fingers twitching hungrily over her pulse rifle stock. If this raider class had the firepower to carve open the derelict...

"We aren't going to outrun that if they decide we're a threat." Dread slithered through Mercer's chest at the prospect, heavier than the gravity pulling at him. "Not in our crippled state. You ready for company, Vex?"

She snorted. "God help me, I was born for chaos. This should be fun." Her eyes burned with feral intensity as she leveled the weapon, scanning for any sign of movement amidst the approaching ship's shadows. "If you can wriggle us closer to that wreck without getting our asses blown to Kingdom Come, do it fast. We might yet salvage something—" 

Their gazes met and held across mere meters, an instant of wordless understanding passing between strangers bound together by dire circumstance. Mercer nodded curtly and began hauling himself onward once again, muscles straining beneath his own suit. In a deadly game of cosmic hide-and-seek, they'd need to improvise...and pray like Hell this audacious gamble paid off before they became its most tragic casualties.

# Chapter 16: Atmospheric Skim

Leo fought gravity every step of the way back to the cockpit, the battered derelict's skeletal frame offering precarious handholds. The distant thunder of the corsair's engines swelled ever louder as Astrodyne drifted nearer, tantalizing glimpses of chrome-and-steel hull painting herself against starscapes.

A stray flash illuminated Astrid awaiting his return, teeth bared in a savage grin as she tracked some unseen menace. Her eyes widened as he clambered in beside her and slammed the hatch shut behind a deft kick. Without preamble, Leviathan strained against tether lines, thrusters roaring defiantly as he fed them everything Solar Wind could muster.

"Hold on!" Mercer bellowed above the racket. Astrid merely flashed a crazed thumbs-up. As Leviathan leapt forward, they surged across starlit darkness toward the waiting derelict's shadow.

Kaelus' thick hydrogen-helium atmosphere began making itself known - the airglow intensified from wispy tendrils to blazing aurorae dancing across the canopy. Radiant curtains swept past, casting iridescent flickers on faces pinched resolutely against impending doom.

"Dive, dive, stay down--" The command came breathless amidst growls of strain as thrusters screamed in protest, spewing smoke trails that bloomed and faded like short-lived constellations.

The corsair's missile lock warnings shrieked insistently atop a cacophony of klaxons and flashing amber lights. A moment later, the night was turned to day as a volley of flares erupted around them, searing vision and filling screens with strobing light.

"Beautifully painful," Astrid quipped acidly, squinting through narrowed eyelids as another flare detonated mere meters away. For the merest heartbeat, she imagined it engulfed them whole, leaving behind naught but drifting, crisped corpses...

Her stomach lurched cruelly as instinct screamed: Fall! Though gravity dragged mercilessly at their weightless forms inside the capsule, Astrid grabbed the release mechanism with numb fingers – no time for hesitation – yanking the lever to sever Leviathan from the tether lines.

The sudden abandonment left them plummeting into Kaelus like a rock, the very atmosphere it seemed cruel to so abruptly deny them now whipping up in a frenzy of buffeting winds and screaming pressure.

Mercer clung to the grip handles like a man possessed, feeling the g-forces slowly bleeding out as they pierced deeper into the unyielding blue depths. Outside the viewport, indistinct shapes blurred into streaks racing past in dizzying shades of azure and scarlet.

"Damn, Leo, what was that?"

"We ditched the tether to get under their radar--"

"So we're just gonna—

–HANG ON!!"

Leviathan struck a turbulent pocket of wind at terminal velocity and bucked violently, throwing both occupants against restraints. Astrid heard something crack ominously in the cabin, pain shooting through her wrist as impact shock rebounded numbingly through the metal alloy shell.

For a fraught eternity, they careered uncontrollably within a churning maelstrom of wind shear, a flimsy husk tossed at the mercy of elements far more violent than even the ravages of war.

Finally, Solar Wind managed to tame their descent somewhat – the brutal jolts giving way to gentle retardation as atmospheric heat glowed fiercely along Leviathan's blistered skin.

Tumbling lazily, merciful gravity once again claimed them as the last wisps of atmosphere sloughed away, exposing starlight to the pitted, scorched hull.

✦ ✦ ✦

Leviathan drifted like a wounded bird, silhouetted starkly against the velvet blackness. Shaken but intact, it bobbed to a stop at a geosynchronous altitude above its target planet—a bruised and livid orb wracked by cyclical storms.

As Astro's head cleared and a throbbing ache pulsed through her dislocated shoulder, she squinted at her copilot's profile through the gloom.

"Humor me, Test Pilot," Vex rasped, struggling upright. Clumsily readjusting her harness, she rotated to face him. The ship pitched gently in response to the correction. "Why in Hades didn't you strap yourself down during that wild ride?"

Mercer braced himself against the console for balance. "I wanted to stay ready in case we needed to eject or make evasive maneuvers." He fixed her with a pointed look. "Your plan relied on the speed to outrun whatever defenses might have detected us—speed I couldn't deliver harnessed up tighter than a corpse."

Astro bit back a wry observation about corpses before forcing out a brittle chuckle. "Fair point." She glanced around at the scattered tools and torn instrumentation. "However... maybe we could spring for some sturdier gear next time instead of scrounging odds 'n ends?"

The pilot smirked. "Not exactly the priority budget can afford right now." His expression sobered rapidly as he surveyed the damage in earnest. "Speaking of which..." Drawing out his comms link, he punched in a coded frequency. "Mercer to Ares," he called crisply. 

Silence stretched uncomfortably, punctuated only by distant thrumming echoes of engines winding up elsewhere in orbit.

After a full minute, he tried again—and received no reply. A chill of foreboding crept across Mercer's nape. This wasn't good.

Vex tracked his griming expression as if sensing it without his voice. Whatever the omens portended, they faced it together within the confined space of command. No matter how much history divided them, right now Astro and the pilot shared an uneasy truce forged of equal parts necessity and distrust.

"You worryin'?" she ventured, leaning close enough to share breathable warmth inside his helmet.

He nodded once, curt and affirmative.

"Well shit, Leo, so am I."

With a low, bitter laugh, Mercer flicked off the comm link. As starlight painted his features somber, Astrid knew this fragile equilibrium between duty and desire was on shaky ground indeed.

"Try to put it out your mind," she suggested mildly, though her voice trembled with uncertain reassurance. "Whatever news Ares has... we'll handle it."

A heavy sigh escaped through his visor. "Just keep telling yourself that, Vex. Meanwhile ..." Frowning, Mercer began running diagnostics on Leviathan's wounded systems. The storm battered mercilessly outside as the unlikely duo braced themselves on opposite sides of the void within. Only one thing was certain:

Their greatest challenges lay ahead, each waiting on the wings of tomorrow or beyond in the infinite expanse of space, where a single misstep could mean eternal annihilation amidst the uncaring stars.

✦ ✦ ✦

Mercer struggled against the relentless drumbeat reverberating through Leviathan's bowels - the ship's lifeblood, thrumming machinery, screeching alloy stressed to its breaking point, groaning struts, and distant detonations rippling their way like thunderclaps across a shattered cityscape. Every shock resounded through his boots and the metal deckplates beneath, making the task at hand both physically demanding and mentally grueling.

With each passing heartbeat, uncertainty seeped deeper into the marrow of his bones, until even the cold metallic chill of his suit couldn't quell the insidious dread slithering through him unbidden. Not for nothing had he honed himself into a finely-tuned instrument of precision and control during years spent honing pilot skills at Edwards Air Force Base. Yet in this brutal crucible only moments ago, all those painstaking repetitions were swallowed by an abyssan nightmare he'd never imagined possible.

And now? Now mere survival hung precariously in balance against the tempest raging without - each gust threatening catastrophic overload to their already damaged propulsion. His fingers flew across the controls in the cramped, featureless flight compartment, working frantically along with Naomi to troubleshoot the mounting list of red herrings flashing through the console displays. If either the AI's vast processing power or Mercer's decades-honed instincts failed them, the result would be more than just an inconvenient delay.

It meant oblivion.

Their voices rose as tensions spiked, punctuated by curses aimed squarely at the malfunctioning nacelles and temperamental fusion reactors refusing to obey commands. Time lost all meaning as Mercer focused entirely on problem-solving.

Then came that singular instant, indistinguishable from countless others yet somehow utterly disparate. In the chaos of flickering screens and screaming gasket leaks, a blinding jolt of awareness pulsed down Mercury's sinewy spine - a gut-level certainty of Astrid standing beside him, just steps away despite the distance separating pilot and copilot.

He glanced up to find icy blue eyes fixed intently upon his features. Close enough for her breath to ghost across his face shield like stolen summer mist, yet worlds apart emotionally. There, suspended within the maelstrom, stood the mercurial heart of their partnership - an unspoken accord rooted in trust tempered by wariness, desire tempered by pragmatism.

Without a word, their hands instinctively met, clenching solid around each other's wrist as if to anchor against the torrent of impending doom. A spark leaped across contact, electrifying nerve endings and short-circuiting rational thought.

In that moment, the vast galaxy receded until only two people existed among unfathomable cosmos - two souls bound by circumstance and common purpose, drawn inexorably towards one another like magnets repelling yet yearning for cohesion.

Astrid's gloved fingers tightened, her touch sending heat blossoming beneath armored layers of skin and synthetic tissues. Mercy, he thought hazily, his pulse racing, his body responding to hers even as his brain shrieked warnings about propriety and professional boundaries.

"I've got you," Vex breathed, an unspoken vow hanging heavy in the air as unseen energies crackled and danced between them unchecked. And in that timeless instant, neither mercenary nor spook truly comprehended how the boundaries between duty and debauchery blurred, until they faded altogether like mist before a merciless sun.

There seemed no end to what they might learn about each other amidst the din of catastrophe, their secrets unfolding in snatches between crises - tales of past loves and bitter heartbreaks, of dreams brutally crushed and defiant remembrances carved in scar tissue and steeled resolve.

✦ ✦ ✦

The fragile electric connection between them snapped without warning, plunging them both back into grim reality at once. Vortex winds slammed the crippled starship out of its doomed orbit, the Marauder careening wildly toward the swirling vortex rim of a colossal black hole. Against the backdrop of hungry event horizon and accreting matter, the ship was little more than a bug hurtling into the maw of a predator.

Leo gripped the console tight enough to put white knuckles against the matte-black surface. His eyes darted frantically across readouts as the vessel shuddered under torquing accelerations. Overhead displays flickered out then flared back on, painting the curved ceiling in strobing curtains of emergency code.

"This can't be happening," Astrid's voice cut through the chaos. She braced a hand against the cockpit bulkhead, her gaze riveted to the holographic navigation schematic. A latticework of projected vectors and trajectory lines dissolved into madness as the ship's predicted path diverged from any sane escape plan.

"We're going to die on that doorstep of nothingness, ain't we?" she muttered darkly. But there was no defeat in her tone, only cold acceptance of a scenario both impossible and imminent. Her eyes met Leo's, sparks of steel-gray ice shining within even as fear and adrenaline coursed through veins and quickened pulses. They clung to each other in shared certainty of their fate, bound by desperate trust forged in infernal crucibles.

Outside, impossibly vast swirls of dark energy seethed just beyond visible light. Gravitational waves rippled outward in symphony with hellish aurora discharges and charged plasma that swirled chaotically on the brink of the black hole's abyss. Stars glinted distant jewels lost in limitless heavens as Vortex's titanic angular momentum hurled them toward oblivion at speeds measurable in fractions of lightspeed.

Then, piercing the cacophonous din, came an unearthly siren cry echoing across subspace on multiple frequencies - alien and ancient, a transmission both primal and encoded beyond human understanding excepting maybe for Astrid herself, the lone surviving operative of Sector Nine's most clandestine division.

Recognition dawned on her face, features etched simultaneously by shock and rapture. At her hip, the silver pendant amulet clicked open with a soft hush, revealing micro-textured circuitry within as it pulsed in tandem to the alien signal. An enigmatic smile played briefly across her lips, her eyes fever-bright beneath lowered lids, before she turned to Leo with decision etched on lines graven by countless battles and hardships faced.

"We have exactly eight minutes till impact. Get ready to die, hotshot. Because according to this ghost from the void, Sector Nine ain't done messing with either our lives just yet."
